items.title: Celestial Conjunction Captures Moon, Venus, and Spica Over Poland
items.summary: Planets shift relative to fixed stars in celestial movements known as conjunctions, which follow precise laws of celestial mechanics. An astronomical photo captured in Poland features a crescent Moon above the Tatra Mountains alongside bright Venus. Positioned near Venus is the bright star Spica, located in the constellation of Virgo. Spica, sitting about 250 light-years away, was historically identified as a binary star system containing two massive blue stars orbiting each other every four days. However, recent findings revealed that Spica functions as a triple star system.

items.title: Scotland's Flow Country Peat Bogs Store Vast Amounts of Carbon
items.summary: The Flow Country in northern Scotland features extensive blanket bogs that store massive amounts of carbon. Because these soggy, waterlogged soils prevent microbes from fully breaking down dead plant material, partially decayed matter accumulates into thick layers of peat. These unique ecosystems require abundant rainfall, poor drainage, and low evapotranspiration. Covering about 1,900 square kilometers of the Scottish Highlands, the area represents Europe's largest blanket bog ecosystem and the first of its kind to earn UNESCO World Heritage status. While forests typically store carbon in living trees that can release it when damaged, peat bogs can preserve carbon for thousands of years. Globally, peatlands cover a tiny fraction of Earth's land surface yet store more than twice as much carbon as all the world's forests combined.

items.title: Curiosity Completes Drilling at Nazca Site to Investigate Crystal Forms
items.summary: The Curiosity rover finished its drilling operations at the "Nazca" bedrock location, which features unique disk-shaped and potato chip-shaped crystal forms. Throughout the week, the rover delivered drill samples to the SAM instrument, conducted ChemCam LIBS measurements on various crystal targets like "Ahi Veremos," "Colca," and "Bermejo," and captured extensive Mastcam and RMI image mosaics. Environmental monitoring included dust devil surveys and horizon movies. Friday's plans prioritized imaging a solar eclipse by the Martian moon Phobos, executing nighttime MAHLI LED imaging of the crystals, and driving the rover away from the drill site to resume its southerly exploration route.

items.title: Captured Image Highlights Planetary Conjunction Over Poland
items.summary: Planets appear to wander across the night sky relative to fixed background stars, creating alignments known as conjunctions that follow precise celestial mechanics. A recently highlighted photograph taken in Poland features a crescent Moon positioned above the Tatra Mountains alongside bright Venus lower on the horizon. To the left of Venus lies Spica, a prominent star in the constellation Virgo. Discovered to be a binary star in 1890, recent findings from earlier this year indicate that Spica is actually a triple star system consisting of massive blue stars.
items.author: NASA APOD
items.original_title: NASA Science
items.original_summary: Not all those who wander are lost. A night sky example is that planets wander, and in fact the very word "planet" comes from "wandering star" in Greek. As planets shift relative to fixed stars, they may appear from our perspective to get closer to other astronomical objects. Such meetings are called conjunctions. They don't happen by chance, but follow the precise laws of celestial mechanics. This peaceful image, captured in Poland, shows the crescent Moon above the Tatra Mountains, and bright Venus close by, a little lower in the horizon. The bright star to the left of Venus is Spica in the constellation of Virgo, the Maiden.

items.title: Virus-Like Particles Improve Gene Editing in Pigs and Chickens
items.summary: Pigs and chickens are vital livestock and key model organisms for agricultural, translational, and biomedical research. While tools like CRISPR/Cas9 have advanced functional genomics, delivering these systems efficiently has remained a significant hurdle. Researchers have now addressed this limitation by using virus-like particles as delivery vehicles for genome engineering tools. Testing across porcine and avian models, the team found that virus-like particle delivery successfully enabled high CRISPR/Cas9 editing rates and efficient Cre recombination. In pigs, this worked well across cells, organoids, and oocytes. In chickens, the approach proved effective in cell cultures, tracheal organ cultures, and in ovo environments. Additional tests with reporter and dCas9 variants further highlighted the platform's broad utility. These results demonstrate that virus-like particles provide an efficient, time-saving method for livestock gene editing across various experimental models, benefiting animal health, agricultural productivity, and One Health research.
items.author: Theresa M. Pauli, Theresa von Heyl, Beate Rieblinger et al.
items.original_title: Virus-like particles enable highly efficient gene editing across porcine and avian in vitro, ex vivo , and in ovo models
items.original_summary: by Theresa M. Pauli, Theresa von Heyl, Beate Rieblinger, Sabrina Teresa Schleibinger, Wei Liang, Antonia Schmauser, Mithuoshni Arullmoli, Paul Derrer, Anika Eckstein, Sirradu Jagana, Camila Gatti Corrêa, Krzysztof Flisikowski, Tatiana Flisikowska, Benjamin Schusser Pigs and chickens are not only the most important livestock species for global food production but also serve as key model organisms in various research disciplines. The pig is widely used in translational research due to its anatomical and physiological similarity to humans, providing valuable insights into immunology, metabolism, and disease mechanisms. In contrast, the chicken has become an essential model for studies related to poultry health, animal welfare, and developmental biology.

items.title: Evolutionary Origins of Paired Appendages and Genetic Rewiring
items.summary: A recent study investigates the evolutionary origins of dorsoventral polarity in paired appendages, comparing them to symmetric median fins. Researchers found that the lmx1b gene is located in the dorsal paired fin mesenchyme but shifts to a posterior position in median fins, pointing to the genetic rewiring of an ancient toolkit.

items.original_title: A new asymmetry, an old toolkit: An emerging developmental enigma in appendage evolution
items.original_summary: by Caroline Schwaner, Tetsuya Nakamura Dorsoventral polarity is a key feature of paired appendages, yet its evolutionary origin is enigmatic as median fins, which predate paired appendages, are symmetric. A new PLOS Biology study shows lmx1b is dorsal in paired fin mesenchyme but posterior in median fins, implying genetic rewiring of an ancient toolkit. items.title: Unlocking the Invasion Mechanisms of Cryptosporidium Parasites
items.summary: Cryptosporidium is a major cause of severe diarrheal illness in young children, establishing a unique niche inside intestinal cells. Researchers utilized molecular markers to observe how the parasite invades host cells with high spatial and temporal resolution. The study reveals that the parasite anchors itself through the sequential discharge of specialized secretory organelles before entering the host. Additionally, a single rhoptry structure persists past the initial discharge to function as a conduit for multiple waves of effector proteins. Eventually, the rhoptry membrane transforms into the feeder organelle that divides the host and parasite cytoplasm, offering a clearer picture of intracellular parasitism.
items.author: Allison Cohen, Tim Bergner, Amandine Guérin et al.
items.original_title: The single Cryptosporidium rhoptry sequentially drives invasion and host-parasite interface formation
items.original_summary: by Allison Cohen, Tim Bergner, Amandine Guérin, Maryse Lebrun, Michael Laue, Christian Klotz, Boris Striepen The apicomplexan parasite Cryptosporidium is a leading cause of diarrheal disease in young children. Within the intestinal epithelium, Cryptosporidium establishes a unique intracellular niche in the apical brush border of enterocytes. A structurally complex interface between host and parasite acts as a holdfast and enables protein and metabolite transport. How the parasite invades its host cell and builds the interface is poorly understood. Here, we reveal parasite invasion with high temporal and spatial resolution using rigorous molecular markers. We find that sequential discharge of specialized secretory organelles anchors the parasite within the host prior to internalization.

items.title: Pepti-DrugPhAI: A Multimodal AI Tool for Peptide Drug Design
items.summary: Peptide drugs are promising therapeutics due to their high selectivity and activity, but poor pharmacokinetics often stall their development. To solve this, researchers developed Pepti-DrugPhAI, a multimodal algorithm capable of predicting the pharmacokinetics and toxicity of diverse peptide compounds. By simultaneously analyzing chemical structure SMILES representations and amino acid sequences, the algorithm efficiently handles canonical peptides, cyclic structures, and non-canonical modifications. The model evaluates critical ADMET parameters, membrane permeability, and toxicity profiles while calculating an adaptive suitability score based on biological activity. Tested against independent datasets, the tool demonstrates high accuracy and provides a valuable asset for selecting viable peptide drug candidates.
items.author: Elizaveta A. Bogdanova, Timofei F. Lukianov, Artem V. Chernukhin et al.
items.original_title: Pepti-DrugPhAI: Multimodal AI-evaluator for functional pharmacokinetics and toxicity of peptides
items.original_summary: by Elizaveta A. Bogdanova, Timofei F. Lukianov, Artem V. Chernukhin, Alexey K. Shaytan Peptide drugs exhibit exceptional selectivity for biological targets and high functional activity making them among the most promising therapeutic agents. However, unsatisfactory pharmacokinetic characteristics remain a critical barrier to their implementation. They often become the primary reason for the failure of promising candidates in preclinical and clinical trials. To address this issue, we present Pepti-DrugPhAI – a comprehensive algorithm for the precise prediction of the pharmacokinetics and toxicity of a wide range of peptide compounds. Unlike many existing solutions, the proposed algorithm is multimodal and can simultaneously process both SMILES representations of chemical structures and amino acid sequences.

items.title: Sphinx R Package Enhances Spatial Proteomics Analysis
items.summary: Spatial omics is vital for examining tissue microenvironmental heterogeneity, yet existing tools heavily favor transcriptomics over proteomics data. To bridge this gap, researchers introduced Sphinx, an R package designed to offer a complete spatial proteomics workflow encompassing preprocessing, cell annotation, spatial neighborhood modeling, and functional characterization. Sphinx introduces an adaptive parameter selection framework driven by spatial statistical metrics, alongside computational optimizations tailored for large-scale datasets. The software efficiently identifies distinct cell types and spatial functional units, such as tertiary lymphoid structures, across various tissue datasets including lung adenocarcinoma, colorectal cancer, and mouse spleen. By improving scalability and computational performance, Sphinx enables deeper characterization of tissue microenvironments and spatial organization.
items.author: Mengyi Yan, Xiaoxiu Tan, Zhenhao Liu et al.
items.original_title: Sphinx: An R package for adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling and functional analysis in spatial omics
items.original_summary: by Mengyi Yan, Xiaoxiu Tan, Zhenhao Liu, Siwen Zhang, Yiwen Du, Hong Li, Lanming Chen, Lu Xie Spatial omics enables analysis of tissue microenvironmental heterogeneity, but most spatial tools are optimized for transcriptomics and poorly suited to proteomics data. We developed Sphinx, an R package providing a comprehensive workflow for spatial proteomics, including preprocessing, cell annotation, adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling, and functional characterization. Importantly, it introduces an adaptive parameter selection framework guided by spatial statistical metrics and incorporates computational optimizations for large-scale datasets, enabling robust neighborhood modeling. Notably, Sphinx offers improved computational efficiency and scalability. Across lung adenocarcinoma, colorectal cancer, and mouse spleen datasets, Sphinx robustly identifies cell types and spatial functional units, including tertiary lymphoid structures.

items.title: Investigating Burst-to-Burst Neural Coordination and Rhythm Resetting
items.summary: Networks of bursting neurons drive robust sequential rhythms in multiple neural systems, such as central pattern generators that oversee motor activity. A recent study combines biophysical models of the pyloric central pattern generator with electrophysiological experiments to examine cycle-by-cycle coordination resetting. Researchers analyzed variability constraints of sequence intervals determined by burst onset and offset timing references. The study successfully identified the conditions that prompt sequential dynamical invariants to emerge as robust relationships within a cycle, as well as when these relations reset or span across consecutive cycles during slow modulatory actions.
items.author: Pablo Sanchez-Martin, Irene Elices, Alicia Garrido-Peña et al.
items.original_title: Burst-to-burst information resetting in sequential rhythmic neural activity
items.original_summary: by Pablo Sanchez-Martin, Irene Elices, Alicia Garrido-Peña, Carlos Garcia-Saura, Rafael Levi, Francisco B. Rodriguez, Pablo Varona In multiple neural systems, networks of bursting neurons generate and coordinate robust sequential rhythms, such as those observed in central pattern generators (CPGs) that control motor activity. In this paper, we combine electrophysiological experiments and biophysical models of the pyloric CPG to investigate cycle-by-cycle coordination resetting in sequential rhythms. In particular, we focus our analysis on the variability constraints of sequence intervals defined by the burst onset and offset time references, which structure the timing of the rhythmic CPG sequence cycle-by-cycle. We identified the conditions under which sequential dynamical invariants emerge as robust relationships between specific intervals within the same cycle, and when such relations reset at each cycle or extend between intervals of consecutive cycles.

items.title: Protein Language Model Improves Antibody Binding Affinity
items.summary: Researchers have introduced Ab-Affinity, a fine-tuned protein language model designed to predict antibody binding affinity against target peptides in the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. When combined with a genetic algorithm and simulated annealing for sequence optimization, Ab-Affinity successfully generated candidate antibodies with over a 100-fold increase in predicted binding affinity compared to their natural parental counterparts. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations indicated that these synthetic candidates have enhanced stability and interactions with the target peptide epitope. Additionally, in vitro experimental testing on a top candidate showed increased binding relative to the original antibody. The developers have publicly released all analysis pipelines, source code, and model weights to support reproducibility.

items.title: New Framework Decodes Transcriptional Bursting from Single-Cell Data
items.summary: Scientists have developed PhysInfer, an unsupervised framework that uses a physics-constrained neural network to infer transcriptional burst dynamics from static single-cell RNA sequencing data. The method addresses parameter unidentifiability and model mismatch by employing a physics-informed loss function that combines stationary-distribution likelihood with zero-count anchoring. This transforms microscopic rates into interpretable macroscopic burst-quantity representations of frequency and size. Validated on synthetic datasets, PhysInfer accurately recovers parameters in low-to-medium activation regimes. Applied to mouse embryonic fibroblast data, the tool successfully mapped a transcriptional dynamic manifold across thousands of genes, and its adaptive topology module identified specific genes supporting a sequential three-state representation, offering an improved approach for characterizing gene expression patterns.
items.author: Xiaodong Zeng, Jingwen Zhang, Shan Li et al.
items.original_title: PhysInfer: A physics-constrained neural network for adaptive inference of transcriptional bursting from single-cell RNA-seq
items.original_summary: by Xiaodong Zeng, Jingwen Zhang, Shan Li, Haohua Wang Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has established that gene expression is driven by stochastic transcriptional bursting. However, inferring burst dynamics from static scRNA-seq snapshots is fundamentally constrained by parameter unidentifiability and model topology mismatch. Here, we propose PhysInfer, an unsupervised framework that integrates a physics-constrained neural network with adaptive model selection and parameter decoupling. A physics-informed loss function, combining stationary-distribution likelihood with zero-count anchoring, reparameterizes the optimization from unidentifiable microscopic rates to an interpretable macroscopic burst-quantity representation of burst size and burst frequency, thereby providing an interpretable parameterization for assessing practical recoverability in static data.

items.title: Method Uses Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem to Detect Brain Memory Effects
items.summary: A central question in neuroscience is how the brain balances local and distributed information processing across different conscious states. Researchers suggest this balance relies on memory effects, where a region's future activity depends on past feedback from the wider network. To study this, the team introduced the FDTest, a technique that evaluates local memory effects by measuring violations of a generalized Fluctuation-dissipation theorem. Testing whole-brain models fitted to human neuroimaging data showed that memory structure aligns with underlying brain connectivity. Furthermore, when applied to individuals during wakefulness and deep sleep, the method revealed stronger memory effects during wakefulness, highlighting more integrated dynamics. The findings suggest local memory is a reliable dynamical marker for different brain states.
items.author: Sebastian Manuel Geli, Juan Manuel Monti, Adrián Ponce-Alvarez et al.
items.original_title: FDTest: Fluctuation-dissipation theorem as a test for memory effects in brain dynamics
items.original_summary: by Sebastian Manuel Geli, Juan Manuel Monti, Adrián Ponce-Alvarez, Gustavo Deco, Yonatan Sanz Perl A central challenge in neuroscience is to understand how the brain flexibly balances local and distributed information processing to support diverse cognitive and conscious states. We hypothesize that a key signature of this balance is the presence of memory effects, which arise when a brain region’s future activity depends not only on its current state, but also on past information fed back from the wider network. Here we introduce the FDTest, a method for assessing local memory effects in multidimensional systems by measuring violations of a generalized Fluctuation–dissipation theorem (FDT).

items.title: Tachykinin-like Signaling Modulates Thermotaxis in Caenorhabditis elegans
items.summary: Mammalian Neurokinin B signaling is linked to menopausal thermoregulatory issues, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To study this, researchers utilized Caenorhabditis elegans thermotaxis as a model system for conserved tachykinin signaling. They found that overexpressing nlp-58, the nematode ortholog of mammalian NKB, leads to abnormal thermotaxis behaviors without altering thermosensory neuron temperature responses. This defect is mediated primarily via the tachykinin receptor TKR-1 in specific sensory neurons, and can be partially alleviated by treatment with fezolinetant, a clinical NK3R antagonist used for menopausal symptoms. The findings establish an NLP-58 and TKR-1 signaling pathway that modulates thermotaxis and provides a model for studying conserved circuit modulation.

items.original_title: Tachykinin-like NLP-58 signaling through TKR-1 modulates thermotaxis behavior in Caenorhabditis elegans
items.original_summary: by Moon Sun Jang, Hironori J. Matsuyama, Ryoga Suzuki, King Chuen Law, Yukimasa Shibata, Xiaolin Zhang, Koutarou D. Kimura, Yukihiko Kubota, Masahiro Ito, Kiyoji Nishiwaki, Ikue Mori Neurokinin B (NKB) signaling plays a central role in mammalian thermoregulatory dysfunction associated with menopause, yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish Caenorhabditis elegans thermotaxis as a genetically tractable system for investigating conserved tachykinin signaling. We demonstrate that overexpression of nlp-58 , the C. elegans ortholog of mammalian NKB, induces abnormal thermotaxis behavior without impairing the temperature response of the thermosensory neurons. NLP-58 is expressed in multiple neurons, including the AIY interneurons, a central integrative node of the thermosensory circuit.

items.title: Baloxavir and Molnupiravir Protect Immunosuppressed Hamsters from H5N1 Infection
items.summary: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) poses ongoing zoonotic risks, and immunosuppressed individuals often face severe disease with limited antiviral guidance. Researchers evaluated the pathogenesis of an H5N1 human isolate in cyclophosphamide-immunosuppressed hamsters and tested several antiviral treatments. While normal hamsters cleared the virus, immunosuppressed subjects suffered 75% mortality, prolonged viral replication, and neuroinvasion. In treatment trials, baloxavir achieved 100% survival, shortened viral shedding, reduced inflammation, and prevented neuroinvasion. High-dose molnupiravir and certain combination therapies also prevented mortality and cleared the virus from lung and brain tissues. In contrast, oseltamivir and low-dose molnupiravir showed limited effectiveness against severe clinical signs. These results highlight baloxavir and molnupiravir regimens as promising therapeutic strategies for severe H5N1 infections.
items.author: Andrea Arroyave, Henintsoa Rabezanahary, Ahmed Sahli et al.
items.original_title: Baloxavir and molnupiravir protect against severe influenza A(H5N1) infection in immunosuppressed hamsters
items.original_summary: by Andrea Arroyave, Henintsoa Rabezanahary, Ahmed Sahli, Mariana Baz Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses continue to expand their geographic and host range, raising concerns about zoonotic transmission and pandemic preparedness. Immunocompromised individuals often develop severe and prolonged disease, yet evidence guiding antiviral therapy remains limited. Here, we characterized the pathogenesis and assessed direct-contact transmission of an influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1 virus recently isolated from a human case in British Columbia, Canada, in cyclophosphamide-immunosuppressed hamsters, with normal hamsters included for comparison of infection outcomes and viral shedding kinetics. We also evaluated the antiviral efficacy of oseltamivir (20 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days), baloxavir (50 mg/kg, 2 doses), and molnupiravir (50 or 200 mg/kg twice daily) as monotherapies or in combination (oseltamivir with low-dose molnupiravir) in immunosuppressed hamsters.

items.title: Nuclear Egress Complex Crucial for Kaposi’s Sarcoma-Associated Herpesvirus Replication
items.summary: During herpesvirus replication, newly assembled capsids exit the cell nucleus through a process called nuclear egress, which is mediated by the nuclear egress complex (NEC). While past studies examined NEC overexpression in uninfected cells, its precise function during lytic replication remained unclear. Researchers utilized transmission electron microscopy to investigate nuclear egress in two lytic Kaposi's Sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) cell line models. In iSLK-BAC16 cells, the absence of the NEC led to capsid accumulation at the nuclear periphery and halted infectious virion production entirely. Furthermore, the experiments revealed that KSHV lytic replication behaviors differ between biological models, with one model displaying extensive nuclear membrane remodeling and slower egress compared to the other. These findings highlight the essential role of the NEC and emphasize the importance of studying viral replication across multiple cellular contexts.

items.original_title: Nuclear egress complex promotes capsid nuclear egress during Kaposi’s Sarcoma-associated herpesvirus reactivation
items.original_summary: by Ariana C. Calkwood Calderon-Zavala, Olaide A. Adeyemi, Paula García-Valenciano Rodríguez, Alicia de Pablos Fernández, Nathalie R. Lavoie, Allison L. Didychuk, Ekaterina E. Heldwein During herpesvirus replication, newly assembled capsids exit the nucleus by nuclear egress, in which capsids bud at the inner nuclear membrane forming perinuclear enveloped virions that then fuse with the outer nuclear membrane, releasing capsids into the cytoplasm. This process is mediated by the nuclear egress complex (NEC), a conserved viral heterodimer of UL31 and UL34 homologs. Although prior studies demonstrated that overexpression of the NEC from Kaposi’s Sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) induces nuclear membrane vesiculation and proliferation in uninfected cells, its role during lytic replication remained undefined.

items.title: Bacterial Motility and Pili Influence Macrophage Phagocytosis of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
items.summary: During chronic lung infections, Pseudomonas aeruginosa adapts to environmental and immune pressures, but how macrophages process these diverse bacterial populations remains unclear. Researchers investigated how P. aeruginosa evades phagocytosis by using an attenuated mutant lacking a functional type III secretion system. Through transposon insertion sequencing, the study identified key bacterial fitness factors and discovered that swimming and twitching motility disruptions decrease macrophage uptake. Live-cell imaging demonstrated that motility-impaired bacteria display reduced surface accumulation and unstable attachments to macrophages. Additionally, restoring the type III secretion system showed that cytotoxicity generally drives bacteria-macrophage competition, though a specific non-flagellated, hyper-piliated mutant exhibited surprisingly attenuated killing. Ultimately, the results indicate that swimming motility and type IV pili dictate physical interactions between P. aeruginosa and macrophages, thereby directly affecting phagocytic clearance.
items.author: Tania Distler, Chia-Ni Tsai, Han-Yi Huang et al.
items.original_title: Swimming motility and type IV pili modulate phagocytosis by shaping physical interactions between Pseudomonas aeruginosa and macrophages
items.original_summary: by Tania Distler, Chia-Ni Tsai, Han-Yi Huang, Alice Pellegrino, Aaron Weimann, Zainebe Al-Mayyah, Lucas A. Meirelles, R. Andres Floto, Alexandre Persat During chronic lung infections, Pseudomonas aeruginosa diversifies under selection from antibiotics, metabolic constraints, and host defenses. Macrophages are key sentinels of the innate immune system and play a central role in clearing airway pathogens. Yet, how they process heterogeneous bacterial populations remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how P. aeruginosa evades phagocytosis under conditions that resemble chronic infection. We use an attenuated mutant lacking a functional type III secretion system (T3SS), which reduces macrophage killing, allowing us to isolate determinants of bacterial susceptibility to phagocytosis.

items.title: Host Pore-Forming Protein APOL7C Drives Immunity Against Leishmania major
items.summary: Classical dendritic cells are vital for generating protective T helper type 1 immunity against Leishmania major infections by producing large quantities of IL-12. Although this process clears pathogens, the precise mechanism behind how L. major triggers robust IL-12 production remained unknown. Recent findings demonstrate that L. major infection induces the expression of a host cytosolic pore-forming protein named APOL7C in dendritic cells. Upon infection, APOL7C localizes to the parasitophorous vacuoles containing the parasites and causes them to rupture. This membrane rupture exposes pathogen-associated molecular patterns to cytosolic pattern recognition receptors, which in turn stimulates robust IL-12 production. Consequently, mice lacking APOL7C exhibit fewer IL-12-producing dendritic cells and a weakened Th1 immune response, highlighting a key mechanism by which host cells detect and respond to intracellular parasites.

items.title: Correction Issued for Study on Carbapenem Resistance in Peru
items.summary: A correction has been published regarding an error in Figure 5, panel D, of a previous study investigating carbapenem resistance and antibiotic susceptibility in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterobacterales from a reference laboratory in Lima, Peru. In the original graphical representation, susceptibility values were inadvertently assigned to the incorrect carbapenemase-production categories. The revised publication provides the corrected graphical data for panel D, ensuring accurate visualization of antibiotic susceptibility profiles among carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa according to carbapenemase production status.

items.title: Study Finds No Significant Link Between TyG-BMI Index and Repeat PCI Risk
items.summary: Most patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention have coronary heart disease. The triglyceride glucose-body mass index has previously been associated with coronary heart disease, prompting researchers to investigate whether this index correlates with the risk of repeat percutaneous coronary intervention. Utilizing health-record follow-up data from a community health service center covering a ten-year period, investigators applied logistic regression models and restricted cubic spline analyses to evaluate post-procedure patients, including exploratory stratifications based on glucose metabolism status. The analyses revealed no significant linear or nonlinear association between the triglyceride glucose-body mass index and the likelihood of undergoing repeat percutaneous coronary intervention. Furthermore, stratified analyses based on glucose metabolism status showed no significant correlations. Consequently, the study identified no independent association between the index and repeat intervention risk, indicating that these findings require additional verification in broader prospective cohorts.

items.original_title: Association between TyG‑BMI and repeat percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) risk: exploratory stratification by glucose metabolism status
items.original_summary: by Weiqiang Fei, Feng Yang, Yongbang Zhu, YiNa Le, Shan Wang, Danxia Sun, XiaoXu Zhang Most patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) are diagnosed with coronary heart disease (CHD). The triglyceride glucose‑body mass index (TyG‑BMI) has been reported to be associated with CHD. This study aimed to investigate the association between TyG‑BMI and the risk of repeat PCI among post‑PCI patients, with additional exploratory stratification analyses according to glucose‑metabolism status. Data for this study were derived from resident health‑record follow‑up records of Yipeng Community Health Service Center, covering January 2015 to January 2025. Logistic regression models and restricted cubic spline (RCS) were used to evaluate the association between TyG‑BMI and the risk of repeat PCI among post‑PCI patients, with exploratory stratification by glucose‑metabolism status.

items.title: Family Emotional Synchrony Impacts Adolescent Well-Being
items.summary: Recent research investigated how dynamic emotional synchrony within families affects adolescent well-being. Using ecological momentary assessment and network modeling on 40 family triads, scientists tracked emotional fluctuations across parents and adolescents. The study revealed greater synchrony in positive affect than negative affect. At the person level, positive affect synchrony correlated with higher adolescent well-being and lower distress. Conversely, momentary increases in negative affect synchrony temporarily aligned with higher concurrent well-being and lower stress. Between-family synchrony continued to predict adolescent outcomes even after controlling for general affect levels, highlighting the importance of system-level emotional dynamics.

items.original_title: Emotional synchrony in family networks is linked to adolescent well-being in daily life
items.original_summary: by Saida Heshmati, Jaymes Paolo Rombaoa, Courtney M. Allred, Alexander P. Christensen, Stacey N. Doan Family emotional processes play a central role in adolescent well-being, yet most research relies on dyadic or static approaches that do not capture the dynamic, system-level nature of family emotional life. In a sample of adolescents (ages 12–17), mothers, and fathers ( N = 120; 2,365 assessments), constituting 40 family triads, we used ecological momentary assessment and a dynamic network approach to estimate how emotions fluctuate over time and co-vary across family members within each system. Emotional synchrony—defined as the extent to which family members’ affective states change together—was modeled at both overall (between-family) and momentary (within-family) levels.

items.title: Umbrella Review Estimates Intimate Partner Violence Prevalence in Ethiopia
items.summary: A comprehensive umbrella review investigated the prevalence and predictors of intimate partner violence against women in Ethiopia by synthesizing six systematic reviews and meta-analyses, encompassing 80 primary studies and 43,785 women. The overall pooled prevalence of intimate partner violence was estimated at 35%. Specific forms included 18% for sexual violence, 19% for physical violence, and 27% for psychological violence. Subgroup analyses showed a 32% prevalence among pregnant women and 33% during the COVID-19 pandemic. Key predictors identified included educational status of partners and women, partner alcohol consumption, women's decision-making power, substance use, and pandemic-related income loss. Researchers emphasize the need for stronger policy implementation and expanded survivor-centered services.

Worldwide, about one in three women experiences intimate partner violence during their lifetime. Accordingly, this study aims to estimate the overall prevalence and identify the key predictors of intimate partner violence in Ethiopia. Methods A comprehensive systematic search was carried out in PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and African Journals Online to identify relevant systematic reviews and meta-analyses on the prevalence and predictors of intimate partner violence against women in Ethiopia.

items.title: Evaluating SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro for Recombinant Protein Tag Removal
items.summary: Researchers evaluated the SARS-CoV-2 3C-like protease as a sequence-specific tool for removing fusion tags from recombinant proteins. Testing standard purification conditions, the protease successfully cleaved substrate containing the canonical recognition sequence AVLQSG, while a variant sequence showed no cleavage. The enzyme maintained its activity across diverse pH levels, temperatures, and typical protein stabilization reagents. Furthermore, the cleavage mechanism was successfully integrated into multiple processing workflows, including in-solution, on-column, and dialysis-coupled methods. Validating its practical utility with a modular expression vector and a botulinum neurotoxin model protein, the study highlights the protease as a viable option for recombinant protein processing.

items.original_title: SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro as an efficient endopeptidase for fusion tag removal in recombinant protein production
items.original_summary: by Trung-Duc Nguyen, Gia-Bao Do, Phan-Anh Le, Mai-Anh T. Nghiem, Linh T. Ho, Thuy T. Le, Hong-Nhung T. Le, Tuan-Nghia Phan, Hong-Loan T. Nguyen Fusion tags are widely employed to enhance recombinant protein expression, solubility, and purification. However, efficient tag removal is often necessary to obtain proteins in their native form. In this study, SARS-CoV-2 3C-like protease (3CLpro) was evaluated as a sequence-specific protease for fusion-tag removal using a recombinant fusion protein substrate under standard protein purification conditions. A substrate containing the canonical recognition sequence AVLQ↓SG was efficiently cleaved by 3CLpro, whereas no detectable cleavage was observed for a variant substrate harboring the sequence TVRLQ↓SG.

The enzyme maintained its activity across diverse pH levels, temperatures, and typical protein stabilization reagents. Furthermore, the cleavage mechanism was successfully integrated into multiple processing workflows, including in-solution, on-column, and dialysis-coupled methods. Validating its practical utility with a modular expression vector and a botulinum neurotoxin model protein, the study highlights the protease as a viable option for recombinant protein processing.

items.title: Study Examines Sun Protection Awareness Among Hajj Pilgrims and Nurses
items.summary: A qualitative study explored awareness, attitudes, and behaviors regarding sun protection among Saudi pilgrims and registered nurses following the 2025 Hajj season. Through remote semi-structured interviews, researchers identified five primary themes: the physical and emotional impact of sun exposure, limited awareness and knowledge gaps, cultural attitudes toward ultraviolet protection factor products, practical barriers like cost and availability, and recommendations for improvement. Many participants viewed sun exposure as a spiritual trial rather than a health risk, while ultraviolet protection factor items were poorly understood. The findings indicate an urgent need for targeted education distinguishing heat illness from ultraviolet risks, alongside better access to protective gear.
items.author: Omar Qaladi, Fahda Alrasheedi, Manahil Alhawsawi et al.
items.original_title: Sun protection awareness and ultraviolet protection factor product use among pilgrims and nurses during Hajj: A qualitative post-Hajj interview study
items.original_summary: by Omar Qaladi, Fahda Alrasheedi, Manahil Alhawsawi, Raghad Alluhebi, Abeer Abujalid Background Pilgrims performing Hajj are exposed to extreme heat and ultraviolet (UV) radiation, which pose distinct risks: heat contributes to dehydration and heat-related illness, whereas UV radiation causes sunburn and eye damage and increases long-term skin cancer risk. While heat illness and infectious diseases have been widely studied, awareness and use of UV-protective measures, including sunscreen and ultraviolet protection factor (UPF)-rated clothing and umbrellas, remain underexplored in this context. Understanding both pilgrim and nursing perspectives is essential for developing effective interventions. Methods In this qualitative descriptive study, retrospective semi-structured interviews were conducted via Zoom between 20 June and 11 July 2025, within approximately one month after the 2025 Hajj season, with 16 Saudi pilgrims and 13 registered nurses who had worked in hospitals in Makkah and Madinah during Hajj.

items.title: Elevated UHRF1 Expression Linked to Poor Outcomes in Adult T-Cell Leukemia/Linfoma
items.summary: This study examined the clinical and biological significance of the susceptibility gene UHRF1 in adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma. Researchers performed immunohistochemistry on tumor tissues from 72 patients and 30 control subjects to evaluate UHRF1 protein expression levels. Additionally, cellular experiments using Western blotting, quantitative PCR, and shRNA-mediated knockdown were deployed to observe proliferation and apoptosis in cell lines. The investigation aims to clarify how UHRF1 influences pathogenesis and its utility as a prognostic marker for patient outcomes.
items.author: Ying Lin, Rong-Dong Zhang, Xin-Yu Xu et al.
items.original_title: Elevated UHRF1 predicts unfavorable clinical outcomes in adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma: Clinicopathological analysis and preliminary in vitro observations
items.original_summary: by Ying Lin, Rong-Dong Zhang, Xin-Yu Xu, Huang-zhou Jiang, Ren-Li Chen, Jian-Zhen Shen Background UHRF1 has been established as a susceptibility gene in multiple cancer types; however, its functional role in the pathogenesis of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL) remains poorly defined. This study aimed to investigate UHRF1 expression in ATLL and assess its clinical and biological significance. Methods Immunohistochemistry was performed to evaluate UHRF1 protein expression in tumor tissues from 72 ATLL patients and 30 reactive lymphadenopathy controls. Univariate Cox’s proportional hazard regression model was used to screen the factors affecting OS and PFS, and multivariate Cox’s proportional hazard regression model was used to screen independent prognostic factors in ATLL.

items.title: New Framework Enhances Bubble Feature Extraction in Flotation Froth Images
items.summary: Researchers have proposed a new flotation froth image analysis framework designed to overcome challenges such as bubble adhesion, overlap, weak boundaries, and uneven illumination. The method combines a boundary-aware U-Net segmentation model with a segmentation-guided adaptive Hough transform. In the first stage, the U-Net architecture uses explicit boundary-oriented supervision to better separate adherent and overlapping bubbles. In the second stage, geometric priors derived from the segmentation results constrain the Hough-based detection process to improve bubble counting and geometric feature extraction. Experiments show that the proposed approach achieves high accuracy and efficiency, offering a promising tool for intelligent monitoring in mineral processing.
items.author: Deqiang Peng, Daoguang Li, Qingxia Li et al.
items.original_title: Feature extraction of static foam images based on U-Net and Hough transform
items.original_summary: by Deqiang Peng, Daoguang Li, Qingxia Li, Chenyi Wang, Xiaomin Ma In flotation-based mineral processing, froth images contain important visual information that reflects the operating condition of the process and provides a basis for process monitoring and control. However, conventional machine-vision methods still encounter difficulties in extracting static froth features under conditions of bubble adhesion, overlap, weak boundaries, and uneven illumination. To address these problems, a flotation froth image analysis framework is proposed by combining a boundary-aware U-Net segmentation model with a segmentation-guided adaptive Hough transform. In the first stage, the U-Net architecture is enhanced with explicit boundary-oriented supervision to improve the separation of adherent and overlapping bubbles.

items.title: Instance Causal Multiple Instance Learning Framework Improves Whole Slide Image Classification
items.summary: Whole slide images often have extremely high resolutions and lack fine-grained annotations, making multiple instance learning the standard weakly supervised classification paradigm. However, existing methods frequently overlook confounding factors, leading to spurious instance-level associations that hurt generalization. To resolve this, researchers developed the Instance Causal Multiple Instance Learning framework. This approach integrates a backdoor-adjustment-inspired prototype module during instance aggregation. By using clustered prototypes as proxy contextual patterns, the model reduces its reliance on potentially misleading confounding cues. Evaluations on the Camelyon16 and TCGA-NSCLC datasets show that the framework achieves competitive performance, improves existing baselines, and features a plug-and-play capability.
items.author: Haixing Li, Chao Weng, Wanying Huang et al.
items.original_title: Instance causal multiple instance learning for whole slide image classification
items.original_summary: by Haixing Li, Chao Weng, Wanying Huang, Ming Xu Whole slide images (WSIs) are characterized by extremely high resolution and usually lack fine-grained annotations, making multiple instance learning (MIL) the dominant paradigm for weakly supervised WSI classification. Although existing MIL methods have achieved substantial progress in feature extraction and instance aggregation, most of them overlook the influence of confounding factors, thereby learning spurious associations that impair generalization performance. To address this issue, we develop an Instance Causal Multiple Instance Learning (ICMIL) framework for WSI classification, which aims to reduce the model’s reliance on potentially spurious instance-level associations. Specifically, unlike conventional likelihood-based strategies, the proposed method introduces a backdoor-adjustment-inspired prototype module during instance aggregation, where clustered prototypes are used as proxy contextual patterns to mitigate the influence of potential confounding cues.

items.title: Identifying Risk Factors for Chronic Evolution in Vogt–Koyanagi–Harada Disease
items.summary: A retrospective clinical cohort study investigated predictive factors for the risk of chronic evolution in Vogt–Koyanagi–Harada disease one month after pulse steroid therapy. Evaluating 121 eyes from 61 treatment-naïve patients, researchers categorized outcomes based on fundus results at 12 months. Multivariable and receiver operating characteristic curve analyses revealed that lower best-corrected visual acuity and increased corneal thickness at one month significantly correlate with subsequent development of sunrise-glow fundus. Determining these optimal cut-off values can help clinicians design more targeted therapeutic strategies for patients with acute Vogt–Koyanagi–Harada disease.
items.author: Tetsuya Muto, Shoichiro Kusuda, Masaaki Sakamoto et al.
items.original_title: Predictive factors for risk of chronic evolution in Vogt–Koyanagi–Harada disease at 1 month after pulse steroid therapy
items.original_summary: by Tetsuya Muto, Shoichiro Kusuda, Masaaki Sakamoto, Shigeki Machida, Shinichiro Imaizumi, Tetsuju Sekiryu In this study, we aimed to identify factors for risk of chronic evolution in Vogt–Koyanagi–Harada (VKH) disease at 1 month following pulse steroid therapy. This was a retrospective clinical cohort, single center study. A total of 121 eyes from 61 treatment-naïve patients with acute VKH disease, who underwent pulse steroid therapy and had follow-up for over 12 months were evaluated. Patients were categorized into SGF and non-SGF groups according to fundus outcomes at 12 months after treatment. Anterior chamber morphology was assessed using Pentacam ® , while axial length and lens thickness were measured with the IOLMaster 700.

items.title: The spatiotemporal evolution mechanism of enterprise-led organic agriculture: Evidence from Shandong Province
items.summary: by Yueling Yang, Qiang Wang, Shu Wang, Zihong Yang, Thomas Dogot This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of enterprise-led organic agriculture in Shandong Province, China. Using panel data on certified organic enterprise production bases across 16 prefecture-level cities from 2014 to 2023, we combine spatial statistical analysis, Local Moran’s I, two-way fixed-effects regression, and robustness checks. The results show that certified organic bases expanded substantially but became increasingly concentrated, forming a clear core–periphery structure centered on the Jiaodong Peninsula. Transportation infrastructure, e-commerce connectivity, and GI-protected agricultural products are positively associated with base expansion, while fiscal expenditure shows a negative association, possibly reflecting compensatory policy allocation to less-developed areas.
items.author: Yueling Yang, Qiang Wang, Shu Wang et al.

items.title: External validation of a machine learning model for classifying hospitalization outcomes in Asian elephants across three elephant hospitals in Thailand
items.summary: by Worapong Kosaruk, Pichamon Ueangpaibool, Nawapa Hirannithithamrong, Janjeera Kaew-ek, Taweepoke Angkawanish Classification of hospitalization outcomes in wildlife hospitals may support clinical assessment and resource planning, but model performance can vary across institutions with different case profiles and care practices. This study evaluated a previously developed random forest model for classifying hospitalization outcomes in Asian elephants using temporally distinct 2025 data from three elephant hospitals in Thailand. The validation comprised temporal validation at the original development center and institutional validation at two additional hospitals. Because length of stay was included as a predictor, the model was evaluated as a hospitalization-course classification model rather than as an admission-time prognostic tool.
items.author: Worapong Kosaruk, Pichamon Ueangpaibool, Nawapa Hirannithithamrong et al.

items.title: Spatiotemporal patterns and county-level coordination between sports-related intangible cultural heritage and tourism development in the Wuling Mountain Area, China
items.summary: by Jiaxin Zhang, Siqing Zhang, Junrong Lei Sports-related intangible cultural heritage (SRICH) can support culturally grounded tourism, but its county-level alignment with tourism development remains unclear in ethnically diverse mountain regions. This study examined 71 county-level units in China’s Wuling Mountain Area in 2010, 2015, 2019, and 2024. Geographical concentration, kernel density estimation, and standard deviational ellipses traced the administrative distribution of officially recognized SRICH records. Entropy weighting, coupling coordination, relative-balance diagnosis, and Moran’s I assessed their county-level relationship with tourism development. SRICH coverage expanded and geographical concentration declined, while county-represented density peaks increased within a broadly stable regional configuration.

items.title: Dual-task interference in the drop jump: Frequentist, Bayesian, and waveform analysis of vertical ground reaction force
items.summary: by Huseyin Celik, Pinar Arpinar-Avsar To ensure standardization, reliability, and maximal performance, physical performance tests are usually performed with little to no cognitive load. However, during training and competition, athletes usually perform physical actions while under the demands of a concurrent cognitive task (CT). This study examined the effect of a concurrent CT on the force-time metrics of the drop jump (DJ) and their reliability under single-task (DJ without a CT) and dual-task conditions (DJ with a CT based on simple arithmetic calculations). Thirty-five healthy young participants performed single-task and dual-task DJ trials in a randomized order. Nineteen force-time metrics covering the braking, propulsion, and landing phases of the DJ were compared between conditions using paired t-tests with Holm adjustment and Hedges’ gz, Bayesian paired t-tests, and statistical parametric mapping (SPM) of vertical ground reaction force (VGRF) waveforms.
items.author: Huseyin Celik, Pinar Arpinar-Avsar

items.title: Computational evaluation of chromone–tetrazole hybrids as noncovalent inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 M pro
items.summary: by Oussama Khibech, Salma Kadda, Yousra Hammouti, Said Abadi, Shehdeh Jodeh, Belkheir Hammouti, Allal Challioui Emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants continue to demand orally tractable, non-covalent inhibitors of the conserved main protease (M pro ). Here, chromone-phenyl-tetrazole hybrids were prioritized using a multiscale computational strategy that connects drug-likeness, binding stability, free-energy ranking, conformational behavior, and quantum-level electronic features. The series showed favorable oral drug-like profiles and low-to-moderate predicted acute toxicity. Among the stable M pro complexes, M2 displayed the strongest computed affinity (MM/GBSA ΔG bind = −38.8 kcal·mol ⁻ ¹), driven mainly by dispersion with limited desolvation cost, whereas M4 showed the most direct catalytic-dyad engagement through His41/Cys145-supported anchoring.
items.author: Oussama Khibech, Salma Kadda, Yousra Hammouti et al.

items.title: Viral suppression among adolescents and adults living with human immunodeficiency virus in Ethiopia during the test-and-treat era
items.summary: by Habtemu Jarso, Rameto Asu, Shumi Negawo, Kemal Ahmed, Biftu Geda, Mark Spigt Background Despite progress in reducing the time from HIV diagnosis to treatment initiation, achieving sustained viral suppression remains a major public health challenge among people living with HIV in Ethiopia. However, evidence on viral suppression and its predictors during the test-and-treat era remains limited. Objective This study aimed to assess the rate and predictors of viral suppression among adolescents and adults living with HIV during the test-and-treat era, January 2018 to December 2022, Shashemene City, Ethiopia. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted among 414 patients aged 15 years and older who initiated ART between January 2018 and December 2021.
items.author: Habtemu Jarso, Rameto Asu, Shumi Negawo et al.

items.title: Design, modeling, and performance analysis of a 2-DOF pneumatic flexible wrist with controllable braking torque
items.summary: by Hongbo Liu, Shuo Wang, Wenpeng Xu To address the structural complexity and limited compliance of traditional rigid robotic wrists, as well as the absence of adjustable stiffness in soft wrists designed primarily for flexibility, a two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) pneumatic flexible wrist with controllable braking torque was developed. The wrist comprises three circumferentially arranged pneumatic actuators connected in parallel around a central pneumatic cross-hinge brake, enabling multidirectional pivoting, while the braking torque can be adjusted according to task requirements for pose stabilization. This configuration combines the high stiffness required for posture maintenance during braking with compliant actuation during motion. Theoretical models of the wrist pivot angle, pivoting direction, and braking torque were established.
items.author: Hongbo Liu, Shuo Wang, Wenpeng Xu

items.title: Combined monophosphoryl lipid A and alpha-Galactosyl ceramide adjuvants enhance the systemic immune response to intranasal inactivated influenza vaccination in a murine homologous challenge model
items.summary: by Thi Len Ho, Thanh Tam Pham, Eun-Ju Ko Inactivated influenza vaccines (IIVs) often fail to provide robust mucosal protection, necessitating the development of potent adjuvants for intranasal delivery. This study evaluated a novel adjuvant combination of Monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL), a TLR4 agonist, and alpha-Galactosyl Ceramide (α-GalCer), an NKT cell ligand, to enhance the efficacy of an intranasal inactivated A/PR8 (iPR8) influenza vaccine. In vitro results demonstrated that MPL+ α-GalCer increased the frequencies of CD4⁺ CD25⁺ , CD8⁺ CD25⁺ and CD4⁺ CD69⁺ T cells relative to both the vehicle control and either single adjuvant in splenocyte cultures, whereas in purified dendritic cell and macrophage cultures MPL+ α-GalCer was no more effective than MPL alone.
items.author: Thi Len Ho, Thanh Tam Pham, Eun-Ju Ko

items.title: Cooperative R&D contracts for power batteries under R&D outcome uncertainty and subsidies
items.summary: by Jinian Liu, Haiyan Chen, Yang Cao This paper examines a supply chain comprising a single new energy vehicle manufacturer (NEVM) and a single power battery supplier (PBS), considering government subsidies and R&D outcome uncertainty. An exponential function is employed to characterize R&D outcome uncertainty. The impacts of R&D subsidies and R&D capability on R&D investment, supply chain members, and their expected profits are examined. A comparative analysis of cost-sharing (CS) and revenue-sharing (RS) contracts is conducted. The findings reveal that: (1) R&D investment exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship with R&D capability and a positive relationship with R&D subsidies. (2) Under an RS contract, the expected profits of the supply chain and its members increase with higher R&D subsidies and enhanced R&D capability.
items.author: Jinian Liu, Haiyan Chen, Yang Cao

items.title: General practitioners’ perspectives on treatment decisions and interprofessional care for women with uncomplicated urinary tract infections: An exploratory qualitative study
items.summary: by Andreas Plate, Nathalie Heinz, Thivjan Thiruchelvam, Carla Meyer-Massetti, Stephen P. Jenkinson, Corinne Steinbrüchel, Daniel Drewniak, Stefan Neuner-Jehle, Oliver Senn Background Antibiotic-sparing strategies, such as delayed prescribing or symptomatic therapy, can reduce antibiotic use in uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTIs), yet their implementation in primary care remains inconsistent. Within this context, non-physician medical staff within general practices and community pharmacies play increasingly important roles in patient counselling and care coordination, potentially shaping treatment expectations and treatment decisions. This study investigated how general practitioners (GPs) make treatment decisions in the management of uncomplicated UTIs in women and examined their views on the roles of non-physician medical staff and community pharmacies in supporting antibiotic-sparing management.
items.author: Andreas Plate, Nathalie Heinz, Thivjan Thiruchelvam et al.

items.title: SPA4 peptide attenuates the accumulation of selected damage-associated molecules and pulmonary cellularity during acute Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection in mice
items.summary: by Shanjana Awasthi, Bhupinder Singh, Jun Xie Activation of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and accumulation of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) are hallmarks of infection and inflammation. The SPA4 peptide (amino acid sequence: GDFRYSDGTPVNYTNWYRGE) modulates TLR4-dependent host defense against Pseudomonas aeruginosa . In this study, we investigated the expression of TLR4, major DAMPs, and cellularity in the lungs of P. aeruginosa -infected mice treated with SPA4 peptide or vehicle. The expression of TLR4 and levels of DAMPs were analyzed by immunoblotting and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, respectively. Cellularity was determined in hematoxylin and eosin-stained lung tissue sections by microscopy. Our results demonstrated that the expression of TLR4 and DAMPs, as well as tissue cellularity, were increased in the lungs of infected mice.
items.author: Shanjana Awasthi, Bhupinder Singh, Jun Xie

items.title: HeteroGrad-DT: Gradient Flow Transformer for heterogeneous multi-task offline reinforcement learning
items.summary: by Ye Wang, Donghui Ma, Jiang Li, Lihong Guo Offline reinforcement learning enables policy learning from static datasets without online exploration, making it particularly suitable for robotic control under safety and data constraints. Decision Transformer recasts offline reinforcement learning as conditional sequence modeling. Extending it to heterogeneous multi-task settings is challenging because task representations and dynamics differ, while joint training can suffer from destructive gradient interference. To address these challenges, we present HeteroGrad-DT, an integrated framework that employs task-specific tokenizers and decoupled prediction heads to retain task-native input and output dimensionality at the model interfaces while learning a shared sequence backbone.
items.author: Ye Wang, Donghui Ma, Jiang Li et al.

items.title: Molecular diversity and structural profiling of the EmrD efflux pump in multidrug-resistant uropathogenic Escherichia coli
items.summary: by Svala H. Mahmood, Iman H. F. Alnaqshabandy Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) presents a significant therapeutic challenge due to increasing multidrug resistance (MDR). While acquired resistance mechanisms are well-documented, the genetic variability of intrinsic efflux pumps like EmrD remains less characterized. This study investigated the genomic diversity and structural conservation of the EmrD transporter in ten clinical MDR isolates from the Kurdistan Region, Iraq. Isolates were screened for the emrD and β-lactamase genes, followed by emrD sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and in silico protein modeling. Results confirmed the universal presence of emrD alongside multiple resistance genes. Phylogenetic analysis identified notable local genetic diversity, including a highly divergent lineage (DUH 11).
items.author: Svala H. Mahmood, Iman H. F. Alnaqshabandy

items.title: Colchicine use was associated with reduced all-cause mortality in patients with diabetic gout without prior coronary artery disease: A propensity-matched nationwide cohort study
items.summary: by Yonghoon Shin, Jung-Joon Cha, Ju Hyeon Kim, Hyung Joon Joo, Jae Hyoung Park, Cheol Woong Yu, Minae Park, Yujin Lee, Soon Jun Hong Colchicine has been associated with reduced cardiovascular events in secondary prevention, but evidence for primary prevention is limited. We examined the association between colchicine use and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and gout without prior coronary artery disease. From the Korean National Health Insurance Service database, we identified 48,295 patients with diabetes and gout without prior coronary artery disease between 2015 and 2019. We compared 28,964 colchicine users with 19,331 non-users by 1:1 propensity score matching, which produced 17,337 matched pairs.

items.title: Hubble Captures Dwarf Galaxy NGC 4449
items.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope recently captured the dwarf galaxy NGC 4449, highlighting the significant role these small stellar systems play in the universe. Dwarf galaxies are about one-tenth the size of the Milky Way and contain a few billion stars, making them the most common type of galaxy. Observations show that NGC 4449 and similar dwarf galaxies lack expected levels of oxygen, implying that stellar winds and supernovae efficiently expel heavy elements into space. These tiny galaxies may therefore be crucial for distributing heavy elements—the fundamental building blocks for stars, planets, and life—throughout the cosmos.

items.title: Heavy Rains Bring Drought Relief and Flooding to U.S. Southwest
items.summary: Back-to-back extreme rain events in late October and early November 2026 delivered heavy precipitation across the Four Corners region of the U.S. Southwest, providing much-needed relief from short-term drought. However, the excessive downpours also swelled rivers like the San Juan and Piedra to near-record levels, causing severe flooding, property damage, and evacuations in locations such as Pagosa Springs, Colorado. Satellite observations from Landsat 9 revealed a dramatic rise in water levels at New Mexico's Navajo Reservoir, which surged by nearly 60 feet between September and November to reach 108 percent of its average capacity. The low-pressure system responsible for the storms was fueled by high ocean temperatures and enhanced by ongoing El Niño patterns.

items.title: NASA Celebrates Voyager 1 Reaching One Light-Day Distance
items.summary: NASA is marking a major milestone as Voyager 1 reaches a distance of one light-day from Earth, equivalent to over 16 billion miles, nearly 50 years after its launch in 1977. To honor the event, NASA has organized public participation through a global digital light wave using smartphones to flash Voyager's call sign in Morse code. Additionally, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory will host a moderated panel discussion featuring mission members and leadership to discuss the historic journey, current status, and unique interstellar science gathered by both Voyager 1 and Voyager 2, alongside a preview of an upcoming documentary.

items.title: Foundation Model Adaptation Outperforms Task-Specific Training Across Medical Imaging Sites
items.summary: Researchers investigated whether pretrained foundation models can replace task-specific training for medical image segmentation by adapting the DINOv2 model and comparing it against U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch. Testing across colonoscopy, breast ultrasound, and dermoscopy datasets demonstrated that the adapted foundation model generalized better on every independent external dataset from other institutions. Within the original training distribution, traditional task-specific models remained competitive when training data were abundant and delineated boundaries more accurately, whereas the foundation model occasionally missed smaller lesions. The experiments also revealed that only a small portion of the foundation model needs tuning, with the required capacity dictated by the imaging domain rather than the adaptation strategy.
items.author: Emre Kutlusan, Yongmin Li
items.original_title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
items.original_summary: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch.

items.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
items.summary: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. In medical lesion detection, the scarcity of comprehensive, stan dardized annotations and the heterogeneity of existing datasets limit the development of robust foundation models. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to building a multi-domain foundation model for le sion detection by integrating diverse medical image datasets annotated for both anatomical structures and abnormalities. We first propose a student-teacher training strategy to effectively combine datasets with heterogeneous label spaces, mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and im proving feature learning.
items.author: Sheethal Bhat, Bogdan Georgescu, Awais Mansoor et al.

items.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
items.summary: We present TorchCurves, a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives. Its central operation maps batches of scalar inputs to points on curves represented in B-spline or Legendre polynomial bases, with differentiation through both inputs and coefficients. Curve coefficients can be optimized jointly with the surrounding model or produced by another network. The library provides trainable modules, reusable basis modules, and a functional interface, supporting applications ranging from continuous feature embeddings to Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and functional regression. Its implementation combines classical evaluation algorithms with vectorized PyTorch operations, emphasizing readability and maintainability without custom hardware kernels. Timing experiments compare curve evaluation against NumPy and SciPy and KAN training against EfficientKAN across a range of problem sizes.
items.author: Alex Shtoff

items.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns.
items.author: Zijian Zhang, Rizhen Hu, Jiangweizhi Peng et al.

items.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.summary: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation.
items.author: Ziang Liu, James J. Kim, Yijia Dai et al.

items.title: Solving the SU(2) BFSS model
items.summary: We numerically solve the ground state wavefunction of SU(2) BFSS matrix quantum mechanics. We compare ground correlators against islands obtained using the matrix bootstrap and find agreement up to five significant figures. The power law tail of this wavefunction determines the three-point amplitude, which agrees with the computation of Herderschee and Maldacena. Beyond the ground state, we extract the non-perturbative four-point scattering amplitude using Lüscher's method. In the appropriate regime, we find agreement with the Born-Oppenheimer approximation that yields the well-known $v^4/r^7$ interaction. We also find explicit bound states with positive energies in various SO(9) irreps. These are closely related to the bound states whose existence was recently discovered by OpenAI.
items.author: Kabir Bajaj, Henry W. Lin

items.title: Pyrite Benchmark Evaluates AI Agents in Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking
items.summary: Predicting how a ligand binds to a target remains a major challenge in small-molecule drug discovery. To address this, researchers developed Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark containing 1,500 pose pairs across various protein-ligand complexes. Tests showed that expert chemists using 3D tools and physics-based scores perform close to random chance. To test automated solutions, the authors introduced PyriteRep, a structured representation of chemical and geometric signals, alongside two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner and PyriteFeaturizer. The agents achieved up to 67% and 74% accuracy, respectively, outperforming human experts. Furthermore, LLM-guided feature discovery surpassed direct reasoning, while optimization techniques allowed open-weight models to match or exceed closed-source alternatives.
items.author: Megha Srivastava, Michael H. Lim, Allison M. Keys et al.
items.original_title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
items.original_summary: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical signals. To investigate automated ranking, we introduce PyriteRep, a structured representation of molecular geometry, protein-ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores, and develop two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner, which directly compares poses through text-based reasoning, and PyriteFeaturizer, which generates executable code to construct features for logistic regression, optionally incorporating features derived from LLM subcalls.

items.title: Assessing Connectome Structure-Function Claims Against Unmeasured Physiology
items.summary: Connectome-constrained models are frequently used to claim that a measured biological wiring diagram dictates function, though such models often confound wiring patterns with tuning choices like excitability or plasticity. Researchers tested three distinct estimands using synthetic ground truths, placebo nulls, and three Drosophila circuit models to evaluate these claims. While certain biological conclusions proved robust across protocols, others shifted significantly depending on physiological constraints and model parameters. For instance, models of the fly mushroom body showed that real wiring could either outperform or lose to shuffled alternatives depending on active cell shares, highlighting underlying model inadequacies rather than wiring deficits. The study concludes that validating structural claims requires properly matched optimization alongside data-constrained physiology.
items.author: Yeyuan Liu
items.original_title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
items.original_summary: Connectome-constrained models are often used to argue that a measured wiring diagram outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, and hence that structure shapes function. Such comparisons can confound wiring with how the models are tuned: a connectome fixes who connects to whom, not the excitability, gains or plasticity rates the model also needs, and modellers often tune these until the real-wiring model works. We separate three estimands: physiology tuned on the real wiring and transferred to nulls (P1), each wiring tuned on its own (P2), and P2 restricted to physiology consistent with independent data (P3). The biases involved are known in machine learning (under-tuned baselines, inherited weights, winner's curse); we measure what they do to biological conclusions, using synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models.

items.title: Continual-ARC Benchmark Measures Lifelong Skill Acquisition in AI Agents
items.summary: Evaluating continual learning in AI agents has historically been hindered by single-domain limits and inconsistent comparison scales between memory-based and weight-based systems. Continual-ARC addresses this by introducing a lifelong stream built from ARC-AGI task editions that require no prior domain knowledge, featuring recurring tasks with fresh instances and incoming new tasks. The framework scores learners based on feedback consumption budgets and tests both memorization of seen tasks and generalization to unseen tasks. Testing models like Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.3 Flash revealed that harness persistence generally fails to improve memorization without explicit expert guidance, and harness methods typically underperform simple demonstration caching. However, weight-based learning demonstrated substantial gains on unseen tasks, pointing toward future continual learning applications.
items.author: Daniel Lenton
items.original_title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
items.original_summary: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are paid for.

items.title: Bonbon Foundation Model Exhibits Emergent Capabilities in Molecular Interactions
items.summary: Trained on roughly 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences without task-specific supervision or structural coordinates, Bonbon is a multimodal foundation model for molecular interactions. From a single representation space, the model displays zero-shot emergent capabilities across functional, residue, and bond resolution levels that generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Controlled scaling experiments revealed sharp performance jumps at the largest model scale of 1.6 billion parameters, demonstrating that standard pretraining loss curves do not predict these sudden capabilities. Achieving state-of-the-art binding prediction speeds, prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets yielded a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds, successfully discovering structurally novel inhibitory molecules.
items.author: Adi Mashiach
items.original_title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
items.original_summary: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly.
