items.author: Zhang X, Wu D, Aldarouish M, Yin X, Li C, Wang C.

items.title: Exploring Environmental Influences on Mono(2-Ethylhexyl) Phthalate (MEHP) Exposure in Common Bottlenose Dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) in Sarasota Bay, FL, USA.
items.summary: Phthalates, endocrine-disrupting, persistent organic pollutants widely used in plastic manufacturing, can readily enter aquatic environments and contaminate estuaries. As apex predators, resident bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) provide critical insights into ecosystem health. Prior work documented phthalate exposure in the long-term resident bottlenose dolphin community of Sarasota Bay, Florida, with evidence of temporal and spatial variability, particularly for mono(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MEHP), a metabolite of the commonly used plasticizer di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP). We predicted that environmental factors, such as large-scale storm events, rainfall, and harmful algal blooms (HABs), may influence this variability. Urine samples collected from 138 free-ranging dolphins during 1993-2024 were screened for phthalate metabolites, reliable biomarkers of exposure.
items.author: Warden KB, Dziobak MK, Wilkinson KA, Wells RS, Sandifer PA, Vulava VM, Hart LB.

items.title: Routine foreskin pathology in adults: Low yield, high cost-Time to change practice?
items.summary: Objective This study aimed to determine the diagnostic yield for malignant lesions and cost-effectiveness of routine foreskin pathology in adults. Subjects/patients and methods A retrospective audit was conducted of all adult circumcisions (age ≥16) performed between January 2015 and February 2025 at a UK tertiary centre. Clinical and pathology records were reviewed to identify unexpected cancer diagnoses-defined as cases with no prior biopsy evidence or clinical suspicion. The number needed to screen (NNS) to detect one cancer was calculated, and pathology costs were estimated based on local processing costs and the pathologist workload score for each sample. Results There were 2503 adult circumcisions performed between 2015 and 2025, with 2.6% ( n = 66/2503) cancers detected on pathological assessment.
items.author: McLean KA, Gardner E, Kirkwood K, Shukla CJ, Laird A, Blackmur JP.

items.title: Pregnancy-Induced Hypertension Complicated by Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome: A Case Series of Two Patients.
items.summary: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is a rare but potentially life-threatening neurological complication associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. This report presents two cases of pregnancy-induced hypertension complicated by PRES, both clinically characterized by headache and visual disturbances, with characteristic neuroimaging findings. The clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics of two patients are described. Following prompt multidisciplinary consultation and immediate interventions, including strict blood pressure control, seizure prophylaxis, infection prevention, and appropriate obstetric management, both patients achieved favorable clinical outcomes. No significant neurological abnormalities were observed at the 42-day postpartum follow-up.
items.author: Zhao X, Yan M, Long F, Mumdzjans A, Song R.

items.title: Use of a Multilayer-Structured Polyurethane Foam Protective Pad to Prevent Deformity and Promote Epithelialization in Buttock Pressure Ulcers: Two Adult Cases With Prolonged Bed Rest.
items.summary: Buttock pressure ulcers are highly susceptible to pressure, shear, moisture, and contamination, frequently resulting in delayed healing. Conventional dressings are often easily displaced in this region, reducing their intended effect. To prevent wound deformation and maintain a flat surface, a multilayer-structured polyurethane foam protective pad (ALLEVYN LIFE, Smith & Nephew), typically used for prevention, was applied alongside local treatment. Two male patients demonstrated the effectiveness of this adjunctive treatment. The first, a 65-year-old man with a chronic National Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel Stage II pressure ulcer that had persisted for 2 months, achieved near-complete epithelialization by day 6 after hospital admission and pad application.
items.author: Mamada E, Tokoro S, Fujiyoshi-Ito A, Ogata Y, Tanaka K, Asaka E.

items.title: Symmetrical Peripheral Gangrene in a Child With Plasmodium falciparum Cerebral Malaria: A Rare but Serious Complication.
items.summary: Symmetrical peripheral gangrene is a rare, limb-threatening complication associated with severe infection and disseminated intravascular coagulation. We report a case of a 6-year-old girl with cerebral malaria who developed gangrene of all toes during treatment. Management included antimalarials, antibiotics, supportive care, debridement, and subsequent skin grafting after adequate wound granulation.
items.author: Ahenkan E, Kotoh-Mortty MF, Boateng FO, Donkor KK, Struck NS, May J, Ascofare OM.

items.title: Clinically Suspected Tumefactive Demyelination Mimicking a Brain Tumor in a 10-Year-Old Boy: A Case Report.
items.summary: After cranial surgery, a 10-year-old boy developed hand weakness, numbness, and fatigue. MRI showed frontoparietal lesions; biopsy lacked documented demyelination. Symptoms and lesions reportedly improved after methylprednisolone. Tumefactive demyelination was suspected, but discordant laterality, unavailable antibody testing, and brief follow-up left the diagnosis unclassified.
items.author: Aman F, Ali A, Khan MF, Khan HN, Shah A, Erkin AS, Khan S, Sattar Y, Khalid AA.

items.title: Do Leaf Temperatures Determine Endophyte Composition and Richness in Florida Native Plant Species?
items.summary: Microbiomes play crucial roles in ecosystems, largely through their interactions with plants. Fungal endophytes occur in nearly all plant tissues and can influence host physiology, stress tolerance, and productivity. Although previous studies have examined how air temperature shapes foliar endophyte communities, endophytes may respond more strongly to leaf temperatures, which are often decoupled from ambient air temperatures. Consequently, changes in leaf temperature (e.g., due to global warming) may alter endophyte diversity and composition. In this study, we experimentally tested whether elevated leaf temperatures affect fungal endophyte richness and community composition in six native subtropical plant species from South Florida. Using in situ localized heating of individual branches, we increased leaf temperatures by 1°C-3°C over a 2-week period.
items.author: Tserej O, Hernandez DJ, Rawstern AH, Kiesewetter KN, Almeida BK, Afkhami ME, Feeley KJ.

items.title: Unified Phase Criterion for Band Crossings in One-Dimensional Topological Photonics.
items.summary: One-dimensional photonic crystals (1DPCs) provide a simple and versatile platform for exploring topological photonics. Topological effects in these layered systems have enabled a range of applications in robust light confinement, lasing, modulation, and disorder-tolerant optical devices. Among their underlying band features, band crossings are of particular interest because they represent critical degeneracies associated with topological phase transitions in periodic media. However, although band crossings in one-dimensional topological photonics have been extensively studied, a unified theoretical criterion for their occurrence remains unclear. In this work, a unified phase criterion for band crossings that applies to both TE and TM polarizations from normal to oblique incidence was derived based on transfer-matrix method and Bloch theory.
items.author: Song J, Liu H, Sun C, Qi P, Liu W.

items.title: Adaptive Genomic Variation Across Sub-Alpine Climates in a Keystone Forest Tree: Implications for Seed Sourcing for Restoration in a Changing Climate.
items.summary: A major challenge for ecological restoration is seed sourcing decisions that ensure that restored populations have the adaptive variation for current and future environments. This is increasingly important for alpine and sub-alpine communities where climate change is predicted to be rapid and drive shifts in selective pressures. Selecting source populations representing future climates is an evolutionary-based strategy for increasing adaptive capacity, but requires an understanding of population genetic structure, identification of putatively adaptive genomic variation and an assessment of how these change across the landscape. Using 3978 single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers we assessed the population structure and diversity of 33 sampled populations of Eucalyptus delegatensis from across its distribution, including 22 populations from the mainland ( E.
items.author: Whale JW, Stuart KC, Bruce J, Pickup M, Field DL.

items.title: Focus-Groups as Data Collection and Citizen Learning Simulation.
items.author: Egerer M, Berret S.

items.title: Staged Endodontic Management and Esthetic Rehabilitation of a Fractured Immature Incisor With Failed Endodontic Treatment and Iatrogenic Complications: A Case Report.
items.summary: Managing a previously treated immature incisor with multiple concurrent structural, endodontic, and periapical complications is clinically challenging. This report describes staged surgical, nonsurgical endodontic, and restorative management of a fractured, discolored tooth with a blunderbuss canal, overextended gutta-percha, apicomarginal defect, cervical perforation, and periapical cyst.
items.author: Priya P, Basnet A.

items.title: Genetic Diversity and Putative Origin of the Bait Polychaete, Diopatra aciculata Knox and Cameron (Annelida: Onuphidae), Occurring in South Africa.
items.summary: The bait polychaete Diopatra aciculata is commercially farmed in Australia and is collected as bait in several South African estuaries. Despite its widespread use, the species' geographic origin remains uncertain, hindering management efforts within sensitive estuarine ecosystems. Mitochondrial Cytochrome Oxidase subunit I (mt COI ) data and ddRAD-generated single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were used to gain insight into the origin and genetic diversity of D. aciculata . A total of 204 individuals were collected from an aquaculture farm in Australia and the Knysna, Keurbooms, and Swartkops Estuaries in South Africa. The mt COI analyses supported the monophyly of D. aciculata and revealed lower genetic diversity in the South African population compared to the Australian population.
items.author: Schoeman S, Matthee CA, Hull K, Simon CA.

items.title: Enteric Fever Presenting With Acute Bilateral Lower Limb Weakness due to Para Infectious Myopathy With Elevated Serum Creatine Kinase: A Case Report.
items.summary: Parainfectious myopathy is a rare complication of Salmonella infection. We report an immunocompetent young patient presenting with acute bilateral lower limb weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase. Blood cultures confirmed Salmonella sp. Prompt treatment with meropenem and azithromycin resulted in reducing CK level from 1854 to 240 U/L.
items.author: Khan S, Farooq T, Hussain SF, Rehan R, Usman K, Iftikhar H, Siddiqui HH, Kamal M, Khan H, Sikandar A, Ahmed S.

items.title: Spatial Prediction of Opisthorchis viverrini Infection Risk Using Multi-Source Remote Sensing, Hexagonal Grid Optimization, and Ensemble Machine Learning: A Case Study From Northeastern Thailand.
items.summary: Opisthorchis viverrini (OV) infection is a major public health problem in northeastern Thailand, where it causes cholangiocarcinoma. This study developed a spatial prediction model for OV infection risk in Sakon Nakhon Province by integrating Sentinel-2, Sentinel-3, and CHIRPS data with hexagonal grid optimization and ensemble machine learning. Eleven environmental indices were aggregated using a newly developed Hd index, which identified an optimal hexagonal grid size of d = 2,100 m. Three models-Random Forest, XGBoost, and Multi-scale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR)-were compared using R 2 , root mean square error, ROC-AUC at exceedance thresholds (1%, 2%, 3%), 5-fold cross-validation, and SHAP analysis.
items.author: Littidej P, Pumhirunroj B, Boonmars T, Artchayasawat A, Buasri N, Slack D.

items.title: Eco-Evolutionary Dynamics of Anadromous Alewife Restoration in a Whole-Ecosystem Experiment.
items.summary: Restoration efforts can serve as opportunities to conduct ecological and evolutionary experiments at the whole-ecosystem scale. We evaluated the eco-evolutionary dynamics of restoring anadromous alewives ( Alosa pseudoharengus ) to a lake occupied by a well-established landlocked population isolated ca. 350 years ago. The restoration of Rogers Lake involved the construction of fishways on all downstream dams and the annual stocking of anadromous adults. Throughout the restoration project, we quantified juvenile recruitment, abundance, and growth, as well as hybridization and introgression with the landlocked population. Restoration led to the annual production of anadromous juveniles and the natural return of anadromous adults.
items.author: Reid K, Littrell KA, MacDonald AD, Job K, Gephard SR, Garza JC, Post DM, Palkovacs EP.

items.title: ASI Serves More Purposes Than One.
items.author: Nielsen AS.

items.title: Astragalus Polysaccharide Exerts a Neuroprotective Effect in a Demyelination Model by Alleviating Oxidative Stress.
items.summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune disease of the central nervous system characterized by progressive demyelination and neurodegenerative damage. The accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and the resulting oxidative stress are considered key contributors to myelin injury and disease progression. Astragalus polysaccharide (APS), a water-soluble polysaccharide, exhibits multiple pharmacological activities, including immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-apoptotic effects. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of APS in MS and to explore its potential mechanisms. In vivo, APS was administered intraperitoneally at 50 mg/kg/day in a cuprizone-induced demyelinating mouse model, and its effects were evaluated by immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, and Western blotting.
items.author: Long Y, Wang L, Hou B.

items.title: Experiences and Gender Demographics of Researchers in Long-Term Individual-Based Study Systems.
items.summary: Long-term individual-based studies have invaluably advanced our understanding of animal ecology and evolution. Participants involved in the creation and/or maintenance of long-term study systems benefit from synergistic collaborations, which can provide greater opportunities for co-authorship. We conducted two surveys to collect anonymous data from current and former participants of long-term individual-based studies about leadership structure and authorship patterns as it is unclear whether all participants-regardless of their intersectional identity-derive the same benefits from participation in these systems. Our goal was to collect these data in a less harmful way through self-reporting gender compared to gendering participants/authors by their first name.
items.author: Kusch JM, Greuel RJ, Jeong C, Regan CE, Stothart MR, Colpitts JA.

items.title: A comprehensive review of detection, optical character recognition, and structuring methods for herbarium label digitization.
items.summary: Global herbarium digitization has produced over 50 million specimen images, many of which contain handwritten or printed labels with rich metadata such as species names, collection dates, localities, and ecological notes. Manual transcription of this information is labor intensive, error prone, and not scalable, which has motivated the development of automated solutions. This systematic review examines studies published between 2018 and 2026, identified through electronic database searches and backward reference screening, focusing on deep learning and computer vision approaches for herbarium label digitization. The reviewed methods include convolutional neural networks, transformer-based models, large language models, and open-source pipelines for optical character recognition and structured metadata extraction from historical and handwritten botanical records.
items.author: Abbad H, Ariouat H, Turenne N, Chenin E, Sebaa A, Prifti E, Zucker JD, Sklab Y.

items.title: Differential recovery of macrophage iron deficiency by oral iron formulations determines inflammation and autocrine hepcidin production in iron-deficiency anemia.
items.summary: Exposure of macrophages to iron has been implicated in sterile inflammation through reactive oxygen species (ROS)-dependent cell pro-inflammatory activation. Here, we compare the effect of the commonly used oral iron salt, iron sulfate (FeSO 4 ), with that of an innovative formulation, sucrosomial® iron (SI), on the iron status and inflammatory activation of tissue macrophages in mice with iron-deficiency (ID) anemia. Despite similar recovery of anemia and tissue ID, FeSO 4 treatment, but not SI, elevated transferrin saturation, generated non-transferrin bound iron (NTBI), and quickly corrected macrophage ID compared to SI, with a more pronounced cell transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) suppression and labile iron pool expansion.
items.author: Antypiuk A, Asperti M, Sharma R, Navaneethabalakrishnan S, Jhita N, Pearce Q, Cox JE, Brilli E, Tarantino G, Vinchi F.

items.title: Impact of venetoclax-based therapies on CLL-associated autoimmune cytopenias: A retrospective study conducted by ERIC.
items.summary: The impact of venetoclax-based therapies on autoimmune cytopenias (AIC) in patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is largely unknown. This study aimed to evaluate preexisting and treatment-emergent AIC in patients with CLL treated with venetoclax, focusing on the differential impact of venetoclax monotherapy versus venetoclax-based combinations. In this retrospective multicenter study, data from 1720 patients were collected; 23.1% received venetoclax single agent and 76.9% venetoclax combinations (mostly containing anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies and/or BTK inhibitors). Combination regimens were used in 97.7% of treatment-naïve (TN) patients and 65.8% of patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) CLL. Preexisting AIC were reported in 11.7% of patients (8.7% in TN and 13.4% in R/R, P = 0.005).
items.author: Vitale C, Chatzikonstantinou T, Papangelou C, Perutelli F, Montalbano MC, Bondielli G, Boccellato E, Alshemmari S, Angotzi F, Arguello-Tomas M, Arpas T, Bašić-Kinda S, Besikli-Dimou S, Bołkun Ł, Buczek T, Butrym A, Chapis K, Chatzileontiadou S, Collado R, Cordoba Mascuñano R, De Paoli L, Deodato M, Dimou M, Donaldson D, Drozd-Sokołowska J, Elias S, Ferrario A, Fresa A, Frustaci AM, García-Serra R, Gogia A, González-Gascón-Y-Marín I, Graklanov V, Hryniewiecka M, Huayuan Z, Iskierka-Jażdżewska E, Jablonowska-Babij P, Jaksic O, Kalicińska E, Kislova M, Koren-Michowitz M, Koumpis E, Kubová Z, Labrador J, Lauzzana P, Levi S, Martini F, Mikhaleva M, Minga E, Moia R, Morawiec-Szymonik E, Morawska M, Mulder FVM, Murru R, Olivieri J, Paszkiewicz-Kozik E, Rani L, Roncero JM, Salamon W, Sanna A, Scarfò L, Shokralla T, Šimkovič M, Škerget M, Spasov E, Tranidou A, Tryc-Szponder J, Varettoni M, Visentin A, Vrachiolias G, Waddell D, Wasik-Szczepanek E, Wdowiak K, Wilk M, Wiśniewski K, Witkowska M, Yassin M, Yıldız S, Zielonka K, Albiol N, Brown JR, Bruno B, Catherwood M, Chatzidimitriou A, Doubek M, Gaidano G, Gozzetti A, Gupta R, Hatzimichael E, Herishanu Y, Jamroziak K, Kotsianidis I, Laurenti L, Nikitin E, Papaioannou M, Papajik T, Špaček M, Stavroyianni N, Vos JMI, Wróbel T, Yağcı M, Kater AP, Davids M, Langerbeins P, Stamatopoulos K, Ghia P, Coscia M.

items.title: Azine-NNN-Pd(ii) pincer complex catalyzed synthesis of haloquinolines and their diversification via Suzuki coupling to access ester and acid functionalized quinoline derivatives.
items.summary: Quinolines and their derivatives are an important class of N-heterocycles that exhibit a wide range of biological activities. The development of efficient synthetic methodologies for constructing and functionalizing quinoline frameworks has attracted significant attention. Earlier, it was reported that the azine-based NNN(Pd)-pincer complex (C1) can be useful in acceptorless dehydrogenative coupling (ADC) and the borrowing hydrogen process (BHP). In this work, we characterized the molecular structure and coordination environment of the Pd(ii) pincer catalyst (C1) by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, and subsequently employed the same catalyst to synthesize halogen-substituted quinoline derivatives. The substrate scope was explored using various acetophenone-containing aromatic, heteroaromatic, bulky, and cyclic groups.
items.author: Bhujbal SM, Mahato P, Vaishnav GM, Wani AA, Bharatam PV.

items.title: 2D/3D-QSAR-guided design of novel 1,2,4-triazole derivatives with predicted enhanced antimicrobial activity.
items.summary: The present study demonstrates that the integration of structural descriptors, quantum-chemical parameters, regression modelling, and 3D contour map analysis within a hybrid QSAR framework represents an effective strategy for the rational design of bioactive 1,2,4-triazole derivatives with improved predicted antimicrobial properties. The work may also be regarded as a practical roadmap for further research on 1,2,4-triazole-3-thiols. Our dataset comprised previously synthesised 1,2,4-triazoles that had already shown broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, thereby ensuring a consistent structural core and reliable biological annotations. Structural, quantum-chemical, hybrid, and 3D-QSAR models were developed using structural and DFT-derived descriptors and were assessed by cross-validation, external validation, Y-randomization, and applicability-domain analysis.
items.author: Korol N, Mulesa O, Symkanych O, Slyvka M.

items.title: Encoding stability and dynamics in hydrogen-bonded octameric capsules through amino acid α-position design.
items.summary: How local molecular determinants encode stability and dynamics in supramolecular assemblies remains a central challenge in adapting biological design principles for synthetic systems. Here, we systematically investigate eleven amino acid-functionalized benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxamides to elucidate how chirality, α-substitution, and side-chain architecture control the formation, stability and function of noncovalent octameric capsules. Achiral derivatives lacking an α-hydrogen exhibit poor solubility in noncompetitive solvents and preferentially form extended polymeric aggregates, highlighting the role of the α-H motif in mediating solvation and preorganization of hydrogen-bonding networks. In contrast, chiral analogues retaining the α-H group readily self-assemble into discrete, D 2 -symmetric octameric capsules. Substitution of the α-hydrogen with a methyl group disrupts solubility and capsular stability; however, introduction of long aliphatic side chains partially restores capsule formation, albeit with increased dynamics.
items.author: Perlitius F, Markiewicz G, Gołdyn M, Avci G, Jelfs KE, Stefankiewicz AR.

items.title: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia of the Tongue: A Rare Case Report.
items.summary: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) is a rare autosomal dominant vascular disorder that may involve the oral mucosa, providing important diagnostic clues for dental practitioners. This report describes a 54-year-old female presenting with recurrent bleeding from multiple red-purple telangiectatic papules on the dorsal surface of the tongue. Her history included recurrent epistaxis, severe iron deficiency anemia, pulmonary involvement, and a positive family history. The lesions blanched on diascopy. Symptomatic management using electrocautery excision under local anesthesia with prophylactic administration of oral amoxicillin (2 g) was performed. Histopathological examination demonstrated thin-walled vascular spaces containing erythrocytes beneath the epithelium, confirming the diagnosis of HHT.
items.author: Atarbashi-Moghadam S, Lotfi A, Atarbashi-Moghadam F, Alam M, Baseri M, Baher MK.

items.title: Correction: Smartphone-assisted optical quantification of d-penicillamine in human plasma sample using toluidine blue as efficient chromogenic probe: introducing a novel portable device toward therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM).
items.summary: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1039/D6RA07917B.].
items.author: Nami F, Bahavarnia F, Hasanzadeh M, Shadjou N.

items.title: Cabozantinib Monotherapy for Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Involving Hemodialysis: Two Case Reports.
items.summary: Introduction Data on cabozantinib monotherapy for metastatic renal cell carcinoma in patients requiring hemodialysis are scarce. We present two cases: initiation before hemodialysis with subsequent continuation and initiation during maintenance hemodialysis. Case presentation Case 1 was a 77-year-old man with lung metastasis who received cabozantinib after multiple systemic therapies. Cabozantinib was started at 20 mg/day before hemodialysis; hemodialysis began 8 months later, and treatment continued for 59 months with tolerability-guided schedule modification. Case 2 was a 69-year-old man on maintenance hemodialysis who received cabozantinib 20 mg/day for lung and bone metastases. The schedule was changed to alternate-day dosing. Partial response was achieved, but treatment was discontinued after 4 months because of worsening general condition.
items.author: Nara T, Furihata K, Sato K, Sato T, Honma N, Horikawa Y, Shimoda N.

items.title: Acute Myocardial Injury in Patients Presenting With Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: Prevalence, Predictors, Troponin Dynamics, and In-Hospital Outcomes.
items.summary: Background Upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) may cause anemia, hypovolemia, and hemodynamic compromise, potentially contributing to myocardial injury during the acute illness. Troponin elevation in this setting requires careful interpretation because an isolated measurement cannot reliably distinguish acute injury from elevation without qualifying change or establish myocardial infarction. The frequency, temporal evolution, and clinical significance of acute myocardial injury in patients with UGIB remain incompletely characterized. This prospective multicenter study evaluated its prevalence, associated admission factors, serial troponin dynamics, and relationship with in-hospital outcomes, including subsequent mortality among patients surviving the first 24 hours. Methods This prospective multicenter observational cohort study enrolled 1,000 adults at tertiary care hospitals in Punjab, Pakistan, between January 2025 and August 2026.
items.author: Abbas N, Shahid FN, Amjad R, Amjad MW, Arooj SS, Sehrish S, Bashir A, Yusuf M, Shafiq A, Mahmood S.

items.title: Safety evaluation of an extension of use of the food enzyme phospholipase A1 from a genetically modified Aspergillus oryzae strain NZYM-LJ.
items.summary: The food enzyme phospholipase A1 (phosphatidylcholine 1-acylhydrolase; EC 3.1.1.32) is produced with the genetically modified Aspergillus oryzae strain NZYM-LJ by Novozymes A/S. The safety evaluation of this food enzyme was evaluated previously, and it did not give rise to safety concerns when used in one food manufacturing process. Subsequently, the applicant has requested to extend its use to include three additional processes. In this assessment, EFSA updated the safety evaluation of this food enzyme when used in a total of four food manufacturing processes. The dietary exposure was calculated to be up to 1.020 mg of total organic solids (TOS)/kg body weight (bw) per day in European populations.
items.author: EFSA Panel on Food Enzymes (FEZ), Zorn H, Barat Baviera JM, Bolognesi C, Catania F, Gadermaier G, Greiner R, Mayo B, Mortensen A, Roos YH, Solano MLM, Van Loveren H, Vernis L, Podea PV, Cavanna D, Liu Y, Tokić V.

items.title: Tunable electronic, mechanical, magnetic, and thermomagnetic properties of Rb 2 CoBCl 6 (B = Ag, Mo) double perovskites: a DFT and Monte Carlo study.
items.summary: The structural, mechanical, electronic, magnetic, and temperature-dependent magnetic properties of Rb 2 CoAgCl 6 and Rb 2 CoMoCl 6 double perovskites (space group Fm 3̄ m , No. 225) were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and Monte Carlo simulations. The optimized lattice parameters were found to be 9.983 Å for Rb 2 CoAgCl 6 and 9.958 Å for Rb 2 CoMoCl 6 , while phonon calculations confirmed the dynamical stability of both compounds. Formation energy calculations confirm that both compounds are thermodynamically stable relative to their constituent elements. The calculated elastic constants satisfied the Born stability criteria, confirming their mechanical stability.
items.author: Abu-Rajouh S, Alkhalidi H, Obeidat A.

items.title: Temporal Progression of Prior Precision, Surprisal, Model Updating and Tone Adaptation in Human Auditory Cortices
items.summary: Auditory perception emerges from the continuous integration of incoming acoustic signals with statistical predictions, a process complemented by simpler local adaptation. Yet, how all these concurrent mechanisms unfold in time remains underexplored. Using magnetoencephalography (MEG) in participants listening to stochastic tone sequences with periodically shifting inferential statistics, we modelled the temporal, spatial, and spectral dynamics of stimulus-specific repetition suppression, surprisal, model updating, and prior precision. By concurrently tracking these computational parameters within this dynamic auditory environment, we revealed a distinct chronological hierarchy governing predictive and adaptive processing. Prior precision states - reflecting expectations - emerged earliest, followed by rapid and concurrent repetition suppression and surprisal - reflecting local acoustic attenuation and global mismatch detection.
items.author: van Haren, J. J. G., de Lange, F. P., Kotz, S. A. et al.

items.title: Ranging and territoriality in African Apes
items.summary: Intergroup relations vary strikingly among African apes, with only chimpanzees showing intense, often lethal territoriality. The economic defendability hypothesis proposes that such territorial behaviour is favored where home ranges can be economically defended, as indexed by the ratio of daily travel distance to home range diameter. To test this idea, we compiled and analyzed comparable data on yearly home range size, daily travel distance and defendability indices from one population of each nonhuman African ape species and integrated these with comparable published data. We find that bonobos had substantially larger home ranges and longer daily travel distances than chimpanzees and gorillas, contradicting a prevailing assumption that bonobos experience higher or more reliable food abundance.
items.author: Surbeck, M., Supple, R., Massaro, A. P. et al.

items.title: Structural Basis for Human Milk Oligosaccharides Recognition by Evolutionarily Dominant Norovirus Genogroup II Genotypes
items.summary: Human noroviruses are a major cause of acute gastroenteritis. Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) contain glycan motifs similar to histo-blood group antigens and may act as soluble decoys that reduce viral attachment. However, the molecular basis of HMO recognition by the P domain of the major capsid protein VP1 of different norovirus genotypes is not fully understood. Here, we combined ligand-based and protein-based NMR experiments with X-ray crystallography to study HMO binding to the P domain of the latent GII.2, dominant GII.4 and emerging GII.17 noroviruses genotypes. Screening of 12 HMOs by STD NMR showed binding of all fucosylated HMOs to GII.4 and GII.17 and none for non-fucosylated HMOs.
items.author: Pisapia, L., Flatau, H. N., Lin, S. et al.

items.title: PREMISE: A Quality-Aware Probabilistic Framework for High-Resolution Source Assignment in Metagenomic Sequencing
items.summary: Metagenomic applications, from influenza A virus (IAV) subtype tracking to bacterial strain resolution, frequently require sub-species resolution.However, traditional $k$-mer-based methods fragment reads into short $k$-mers and discard per-base quality scores.By omitting both intra-read linkage and error information, these methods confound closely related genomic variants, thereby impeding real-time pathogen surveillance and containment.We introduce \premise (Pathogen Resolution via Expectation-Maximization In Sequencing Experiments), a probabilistic, alignment-based framework implemented in Rust for high-resolution source assignment against near-complete reference databases.\premise aligns whole reads using a bidirectional run-length FM-index and quantifies reference abundances with a quality-aware Expectation-Maximization algorithm mapped over a taxonomy.This framework applies an optional sparsity penalty to resolve ambiguous assignments, which is particularly important when sparse samples are mapped against reference databases rich in highly homologous candidate references.On ten dense CAMI II strain-madness samples, \premise achieves the highest species-level read classification F1 score ($0.992$) among eight evaluated methods, with no false-positive or missed species.At…
items.author: Vijendran, S., Dorman, K., Anderson, T. K. et al.

items.title: Mathematical model of phenotypic plasticity predicts interconversion is a drug target for neuroblastoma.
items.summary: Neuroblastoma is a paediatric cancer arising from the sympathetic nervous system as neural crest cells, made up of noradrenergic (NOR/ADRN/N), mesenchymal like (MES/S), and intermediate (I-type/I) cell types. These cells can interconvert between types, contributing to treatment resistance and relapse. We developed a mathematical model to investigate how interconversion patterns affect the efficacy of phenotype-specific inhibitors. We used three ordinary differential equations to describe the dynamics of the three populations, including logistic growth, interconversion, and drug-induced death. Of the 64 possible interconversion patterns, five reduced the target population: two for N cells and three for S cells. N targeting patterns were more effective with higher interconversion rates, while mesenchymal targeting patterns were more effective with lower interconversion rates.
items.author: Covell, F., Patel, M., Wertheim, K. Y.

items.title: Residual Hearing Loss After Chronic Cochlear Implantation in Guinea Pigs is Primarily Conductive
items.summary: It is desirous to preserve residual low-frequency hearing in cochlear implant recipients, as dual stimulation using electrical and acoustic signals results in superior speech-in-noise processing and musicality. However, cochlear implant recipients commonly lose their residual acoustic hearing gradually following surgical placement of the array. The governing mechanism is not understood and is likely due to multiple factors including surgical trauma, inflammation, and the foreign body induced immune response to the array, including formation of intracochlear fibrosis. Normal mechanical function of the cochlea is expected to underpin residual hearing but has not been directly studied. This function includes efficient transmission of sound to the cochlea via the middle ear, sound propagation via the basilar membrane travelling wave, mechanical tuning characteristics, and the non-linear cochlear amplification of responses to low-frequency stimulation.
items.author: He, W., Xing, R., Hill, J. D. et al.

items.title: β-cell NCK1 is reduced in type 2 diabetes, impairing the unfolded protein response and insulin secretion while revealing sex-specific adaptation
items.summary: Type 2 diabetes is characterized by failure of pancreatic {beta} cells to adapt insulin secretion to metabolic demand, causing {beta} cell function and reduced {beta} cell mass. The unfolded protein response (UPR) is central to adaptation by maintaining endoplasmic reticulum homeostasis and supporting insulin biosynthesis, secretion, proliferation, and survival. NCK1, is an adaptor protein that regulates insulin biosynthesis and UPR activation, positioning it at the crossroads of several processes essential for {beta} cell function. We found in mouse and human islets that NCK1 expression was upregulated by glucose and reduced in individuals living with type 2 diabetes. We thus explored the importance of {beta} cell NCK1 in endocrine function and glucose homeostasis using INS 1 cells, mouse and human islets, and {beta} cell specific knockout male and female mice (NCK1{beta}KO).
items.author: Monteillet, L., Jouvet, N., Huet, R. et al.

items.title: Secondary growth in the tomato stem is suppressed by the flowering regulators FUL2 and STM3
items.summary: Herbaceous eudicot crops such as tomato accumulate substantial amounts of secondary xylem in their stems, particularly in the basal part. As plants progress from the vegetative phase to flowering and fruit development, secondary growth continues to provide mechanical support and facilitate transport. To uncover how secondary growth is regulated in the tomato stem, we used laser capture microdissection RNA-seq to establish tissue-specific transcriptomic profiles. This revealed that key regulators associated with wood formation in poplar are also acting in tomato. Furthermore, we found that the flowering regulators FUL2 and STM3 are substantially expressed in xylem tissue. Subsequent functional analysis identified FUL2 and STM3 as key repressors of secondary growth, with ful2 or stm3 knock-out mutants exhibiting strongly increased secondary growth in older tomato stems.
items.author: Pandey, K., Appiah, A. P., van Velzen, R. et al.

items.title: A three-factor model can explain symmetry breaking and the n-1 rule during X-chromosome inactivation
items.summary: X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) is a mammalian gene regulatory process that via chromosome-scale transcriptional silencing, leaves active a single X chromosome per diploid genome complement. The mechanisms that enable cells to select the appropriate number of X chromosomes to inactivate while leaving others active remain unclear. We demonstrate that all known chromosomal counting scenarios during XCI can be accounted for by a three-factor mathematical model that includes (1) Xist, the long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) responsible for gene silencing during XCI in eutherians, (2) an X-linked transcriptional activator of Xist, and (3) the autosomally-encoded SPEN, an Xist RNA-binding protein that is essential for gene silencing during XCI.
items.author: Guan, K., Liu, J. M., Calabrese, J. M. et al.

items.title: Auditory Evoked Potentials Differ from Controls and Correlate with Aspects of Cognition in Kabuki Syndrome and Rubinstein-Taybi Syndrome
items.summary: Objective Kabuki syndrome (KS) and Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome (RSTS) are two disorders caused by dysfunctional components of the epigenetic machinery and both result in intellectual disability. Mouse models of both KS and RSTS have seen reversal of cognitive impairment with epigenetic treatments. However, a great need exists for biomarkers in these disorders to improve the likelihood of successful clinical trials. This study aimed to investigate cortical auditory evoked potentials (AEPs) in KS and RSTS so that it could potentially be developed into a response biomarker in the future. Methods The amplitude of the N1-P2-N2 complex was measured for passive listening to monotonal auditory stimuli in individuals with KS, with RSTS, and typically developing controls.
items.author: Kalinousky, A., Bucklin, E., Ng, R. et al.

items.title: Modeling circadian rhythm splitting under chronic light and the asymmetric transition kinetics between lighting conditions
items.summary: In various vertebrates, chronic light splits the single daily 24-h circadian activity bout into two 12-h behavioral components per cycle, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we develop a two-lobe biophysical model of the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) to understand this phenomenon. By representing the master clock as interacting ventral core and dorsal shell populations of Kuramoto-type oscillators across bilateral lobes, we suggest that chronic light changes the excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance orchestrated by GABA, which either inhibits or excites SCN neurons. Under constant darkness, excitation dominates and provides in-phase synchronization of the populations. Under chronic light, inhibition dominates, and the ipsilateral and contralateral couplings among the core and shell populations become negative.
items.author: Goltsev, A. V., Mendes, J. F.

items.title: Robust lesion network mapping reveals symptom-specific circuits
items.summary: Lesion network mapping (LNM) is a powerful tool for linking distributed brain lesions to symptom-relevant networks, but similar LNM maps across unrelated symptoms have raised concerns about its statistical validity and specificity. Here we introduce robust LNM (rLNM), a statistically principled framework that combines two complementary controls: an anatomy-preserving spatial null model to account for connectome-derived hub bias shared across symptoms, and hypothesis-driven contrasts to resolve selective specificity among related symptoms. rLNM effectively controls both false positives and negatives. Across 10 lesion datasets (384 lesions) and two task-fMRI meta-analyses (339 experiments), rLNM recovers distinct symptom-specific networks (mean r = 0.044), which show significantly reduced similarity to the connectome hub pattern (r = 0.12 vs.
items.author: Cui, W., Zhu, J., Long, Y. et al.

items.title: Neural transformation from image realism to perceived realness
items.summary: Humans readily perceive whether a visual stimulus depicts something that could exist in the real world, yet the neural basis of perceived realness remains unclear. Because differences between real and unreal stimuli are ultimately expressed through visual features, realness might be expected to emerge along the ventral visual stream. Contrary to this prediction, we show that perceived-realness representations emerge in higher dorsal visual areas through a transformation of image-realism-related image-feature representations in early visual and early dorsal visual areas. fMRI revealed this representational shift toward intraparietal sulcus (IPS), with IPS patterns predicting perceived realness beyond image features and decision difficulty; source-localized MEG showed that realness coding in IPS emerged later than feature coding in early visual and dorsal visual areas.
items.author: Orima, T., Ban, H.

items.title: A Mathematical Model of Reliability-Dependent Sensory Reweighting in Quiet Standing
items.summary: Human quiet standing relies on vestibular, proprioceptive, and visual information whose contributions change with sensory context. Posturography characterizes this reweighting through responses to visual and support-surface perturbations, but a compact account of how sensory reliability propagates from state estimation to postural action remains incomplete. We develop a minimal quiet-standing model in which sensory reliability is encoded by channel-specific precision parameters that weight sensory prediction errors. A one-link inverted pendulum with intrinsic ankle stiffness estimates posture by minimizing an active-inference free-energy objective and selects ankle torque by minimizing the same objective under a restorative sensory goal. A fixed-point analysis predicts in closed form the perturbation-induced belief bias, each channel's state-update contribution, the steady posture, and a linear stability condition from the precisions, goal dynamics, and intrinsic stiffness.
items.author: Kobayashi, J.

items.title: Emergent topological structure in spontaneous brain-organoid activity
items.summary: Neural activity is widely held to organize on low-dimensional structure embedded in a high-dimensional state space. Persistent homology reads such structure directly from the pattern of pairwise correlations, without assuming in advance which variables are relevant. We apply persistent homology to microelectrode-array (MEA) recordings of spontaneous activity from human (Lancaster) and mouse (Pasca) cortical organoids, spanning 25-197 sorted units, and ask whether topological data analysis resolves structure at the node counts that neural recordings actually deliver. Building weighted networks in correlation space and characterizing them by Vietoris-Rips filtration, we find that the first homology (H1, loops) rises significantly above a rate- and population-preserving null in 14 of 18 datasets, all of which remain significant after correction for testing 18 datasets.
items.author: Bodnia, E., Basart, M., Hai, S. et al.

items.title: γδ T cell-derived IL-17A aggravates experimental epidermolysis bullosa acquisita in response to IL-1β
items.summary: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita (EBA) is a mucocutaneous autoimmune blistering disorder mediated by autoantibodies against type VII collagen and subsequent splitting of the dermal-epidermal junction. Interleukin (IL)-17A promotes the production of chemokines and cytokines involved in neutrophil recruitment and activation, suggesting that IL-17A may contribute to EBA pathogenesis. We aimed to clarify the role of IL-17A in experimental EBA. Using an antibody transfer-induced EBA mouse model, we demonstrate that IL-17A promotes disease development, as pharmacological blockade of IL-17A with a neutralizing antibody ameliorated skin lesions. Gamma-delta ({gamma}{delta}) T cells were identified as the predominant cellular source of IL-17A, supported by the attenuated disease phenotype observed in {gamma}{delta}TCR-deficient mice.
items.author: Deng, F., Jukic, S., Wannick, M. et al.

items.title: A noncanonical function of Dicer fuels self-dsRNA-driven inflammation
items.summary: Self-derived double-stranded RNA (self-dsRNA) acts as potent triggers of autoinflammation and damage-associated molecular patterns in cancer and infection. However, the upstream processes controlling self-dsRNA homeostasis remain unclear. We uncover a non-canonical role for human Dicer in driving cell-intrinsic immunity to self-dsRNAs that arise from editing or splicing defects, epigenetic deregulation or mitochondrial stress. Dicer loss abolishes type-I interferon induction, PKR activation, and OAS-RNase L activation in response to self - but not exogenous - dsRNA in multiple cell types, including a clinically-relevant hiPSC model of neuroinflammation. Dicer interacts with G3BP1 and LGP2 to regulate self-dsRNA availability and recognition, respectively, independently of miRNAs.
items.author: ter Haar, L. R., de Lange, S., Gravekamp, D. et al.

items.title: Cell-scale confinement reorders bacterial speed rankings
items.summary: Which bacterium swims fastest depends on where the race is run. Speeds are usually measured in open liquid, yet many bacteria live in pores, mucus and host passages no wider than a cell. Using a microfluidic device with eight channel widths (0.80-3.00 m) in one field of view, we tracked unlabeled cells of eight species spanning five motility systems. Chamber height, a polymer additive and channel width each reordered the ranking. Vibrio alginolyticus, the fastest in open liquid, slowed to ~4 m/s in 1.25-m channels, whereas Campylobacter jejuni and Bacillus subtilis kept 33-46 m/s. Open liquid speed did not predict robustness to confinement.
items.author: Shimada, Y. Y., Uemura, N. A., Yoshioka, A. et al.

items.title: Dual regulation of chemical stress-induced DDI2/3 expression by a transcription factor Fzf1 and nucleosome in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
items.summary: DDI2 and DDI3 (DDI2/3) are duplicated genes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae that exhibit strong induction by a transcription factor Fzf1 in response to chemical treatments like cyanamide (CY) and methyl methanesulfonate (MMS). Although, like DDI2/3, SSU1, YHB1 and YNR064C also contain an Fzf1-binding consensus sequence CS2 and are coordinately regulated by Fzf1, these genes are only modestly induced by CY and MMS. To identify additional cis-acting elements in the DDI2/3 promoter, we made DDI2/3 promoter deletions in a reporter system and identified upstream repressing sequences (URS) spanning 480 nucleotides. To test a hypothesis that the chromatin structure constitutes the URS, we utilized a yeast strain capable of histone H3/H4 depletion by shifting carbon sources.
items.author: Du, Y., Lin, A., Brown, J. A. R. et al.

items.title: ER stress-associated IRE1α signalling links impaired QPRT-dependent NAD⁺ biosynthesis to reduced oocyte competence
items.summary: Oocyte quality is closely linked to metabolic and organelle homeostasis, but the mechanisms underlying naturally occurring differences in oocyte quality remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify a link between endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, impaired NAD biosynthesis and poor oocyte quality. Poor-grade goat oocytes exhibited profound NAD depletion, accompanied by quinolinic acid accumulation and reduced expression of quinolinate phosphoribosyltransferase (QPRT), suggesting a bottleneck in de novo NAD biosynthesis. Restoring QPRT expression or bypassing this metabolic step improved meiotic maturation. Further analyses revealed altered ER stress signalling, increased IRE1-associated activity and reduced QPRT RNA stability. Recombinant IRE1 processed QPRT RNA in vitro, suggesting a possible link between IRE1 activity and QPRT transcript regulation.
items.author: Athar, M., E, A. K., Birajdar, P. et al.

items.title: A Dynamic Stem Cell State Links Environmental Cues to Skeletal and Regenerative Fates
items.summary: Stem cells faithfully generate tissue architecture during development, yet how their identity and regenerative output are reshaped as anatomical niches mature and environmental signals change with aging and injury remains poorly understood. Rare skeletal stem cells (SSCs) across diverse skeletal sites are defined by combinations of cell-surface markers, precluding their genetic interrogation in vivo. Here, using spatially informed single cell transcriptomics, we identify Pannexin-3 (Panx3) to mark a dynamic functional state within bona fide SSCs and establish Panx3-CreERT2 mice for its longitudinal interrogation. Panx3 SSCs exhibit long-term clonal persistence, self-renewal and multipotency, whereas Panx3- SSCs can acquire this state. Successive SSC cohorts engage the Panx3 state during skeletal development, osteoanabolic stimulation expands pre-existing Panx3 SSC clones and injury induces it locally in previously unlabeled progenitors.
items.author: Wang, Y., Zhao, L., Chen, K. et al.

items.title: Proteome-wide profiling reveals compartment-specific RNA buffering of protein aggregation during stress
items.summary: Cellular adaptation to stress requires extensive remodeling of RNA metabolism. The rewiring of the RNA-protein interaction landscape and the assembly of biomolecular condensates are central to this response, yet the global stress-induced reorganization of macromolecular RNA-protein assemblies remains incompletely characterized. Here, we apply R-DeeP, a density gradient approach coupled to quantitative mass spectrometry, to profile the RNA-dependent sedimentation behaviour of the Saccha-romyces cerevisiae proteome during heat and salt stress. We demonstrate that stress triggers a profound, stress-specific reorganization of the RNA interactome. Many proteins undergo pronounced, selective shifts into high-molecular weight fractions, indicative of aggregation. RNase treatment markedly exacerbates this aggregation, consistent with the model that RNA acts as a general chaperone that keeps proteins with intrinsically disordered regions soluble.
items.author: Seidler, J. F., Thelen, F., Wäber, N. B. et al.

items.title: Mutually Repressive Transcription Factors Drive Intestinal Maturation for Weaning
items.summary: In mammals, rapid neonatal growth depends on specialized intestinal enterocytes that absorb nutrients from milk. These cells exhibit distinct functions, morphologies, and gene expression programs that support neonatal nutrition before transitioning to an adult state at weaning. However, the transcriptional mechanisms that establish neonatal enterocyte identity and coordinate their maturation remain poorly understood. Here we show that the transcription factors BLIMP1 and CASZ1 form a central switch in the timing of enterocyte maturation. While BLIMP1 marks and promotes neonatal enterocytes, CASZ1 is expressed in adult enterocytes and is required for the proper timing of their emergence. Genetic analysis indicates that these neonatal and adult factors are mutually repressive, forming a genetic switch underlying weaning.
items.author: Scales, M. K., Karsan, R., Underwood, J. et al.

items.title: Body size cascades from Neodiprion sawfly hosts to Perilampid parasitoids: An investigation of sequential divergence
items.summary: Ecological speciation drives diversity in plant-eating insect systems, but it may also generate parallel specialization in parasitoid associates in a cascading effect of "sequential divergence." However, sequential divergence has never been successfully identified in parasitoids of externally feeding insects. To address this gap, we consider the Pinus-Neodiprion-Perilampus neodiprioni system, where plant-associated, externally feeding Neodiprion demonstrate ecological divergence, as supported by body size as a magic trait in sympatric species. It seems possible that this body size differentiation may cascade to Neodiprion's parasitoids via sequential divergence. Therefore, we asked, "Does P. neodiprioni exhibit host-specific divergence in body size that parallels patterns in Neodiprion hosts?" Further, "Does P.
items.author: White, S. V., Mohammed, S., Bagley, R. K.

items.title: Widespread Saccharomyces hybridization in agave fermentations arises repeatedly from asymmetric parental diversity
items.summary: Interspecific hybridization can profoundly reshape genomes by bringing together divergent genetic backgrounds, yet its ecological and evolutionary dynamics remain poorly understood at the population level. Here, we identify an extensive hybridization system in traditional agave fermentations across Mexico involving Saccharomyces cerevisiae, a species frequently associated with human-managed environments, and its predominantly wild relative S. paradoxus. A genomic survey reveals unexpectedly high hybrid frequencies in geographically distant regions with contrasting environments. Targeted sampling of distilleries and surrounding natural sites reveals a strong ecological bias, with hybrids recovered almost exclusively from distilleries, although both parental species occur in anthropogenic and natural habitats.
items.author: Avelar-Rivas, J. A., Aguirre-Dugua, X., Lopez-Gallegos, C. et al.

items.title: Global homeostatic forces shape the composition of a hyperdiverse tropical insect fauna
items.summary: Despite comprising the bulk of terrestrial biodiversity, we know surprisingly little about insect faunas, particularly in the tropics. Here, we characterize the insect fauna of Madagascar, a global biodiversity hotspot, based on extensive DNA metabarcoding of Malaise trap and leaf litter samples. We estimate that the fauna comprises at least 250,000 species, only 5% of which are currently recorded. The ecological and taxonomic composition is surprisingly similar to that of temperate forests. We show that this is likely caused by global homeostatic forces shaping net diversification rates after colonization of Madagascar rather than by the composition of colonizing lineages. Features differing from temperate forests include the dearth of parasitoids and richness of beetles.
items.author: Ronquist, F., Iwaszkiewicz-Eggebrecht, E., van Dijk, L. J. A. et al.

items.title: Do divergent mitochondrial backgrounds alter the fate of nuclear alleles during hybridization and admixture?
items.summary: Hybridization brings together genetic variation from different populations or species into admixed genomes. As selection sorts this variation, the fate of each allele is determined by its fitness effect in the new hybrid genomic background. Because mitochondrial genes coevolve with the nuclear genome, they may be especially sensitive to foreign nuclear backgrounds, making them potential "hot-spots" for hybrid incompatibilities. Here, we test whether selection against mitonuclear incompatibilities drives repeatable hybridization outcomes. Specifically, we experimentally evolved three sets of five populations of hybrid Drosophila melanogaster, each carrying the same nuclear chromosomes but paired with one of three increasingly divergent mitochondrial DNA backgrounds.
items.author: Darwin, L. J., Bachtel, R. Z., Lemieux, F. A. et al.

items.title: Measuring satellite arrays of the human Y chromosome from sequencing reads
items.summary: Human Y chromosome satellites vary widely but remain difficult to measure in large cohorts. In response, we developed Yruler, which uses pangenome assemblies to measure satellite lengths, composition and Y dosage from sequencing reads without alignment. Analyses reveal centromere-length differences between related lineages, extend observations of short non-centromeric arrays across a lineage, and show unequal component variability and composition changes with heterochromatin length within lineages. Yruler brings satellite variation into population-scale phenotype studies.
items.author: Ortigas-Vasquez, A., Guarracino, A.

items.title: Epigenome-informed Polymer Modeling Reveals Chromosome Folding Landscapes across Distinct Genetic and Epigenetic Contexts
items.summary: Three-dimensional (3D) genome organization is critical for gene regulation, enabling long-range interactions between genes and distal regulatory elements. Genomic structural variations and epigenetic differences can perturb this organization, contributing to phenotypic variation and tissue-specific gene regulation. Prior studies have assessed the impact of these genetic and epigenetic changes on 3D genome folding, primarily using population-averaged features such as topologically associating domains and loops. However, growing evidence from single-cell and live-imaging studies indicates that chromosomes are highly dynamic and exist as heterogeneous ensembles of conformations. Here, we applied an epigenetic-state-informed polymer modeling framework to generate chromosomal conformational ensembles directly from cell- and tissue-specific epigenomic data.
items.author: Bazmi, S., Turco, A., Kumar, S.

items.title: Sexing carnivores from faecal metagenomes: calibrating Rx for stone marten and red fox
items.summary: Knowing the sex of the animal that deposited a scat adds value to non-invasive monitoring, but read-ratio sexing methods were developed for human ancient DNA. We examined their use in shotgun metagenomes of seven stone marten (Martes foina) and red fox (Vulpes vulpes) scats. Human DNA, present in every library, was removed by competitive mapping against the host assembly and the human reference. Applying the Skoglund Ry metric to the marten samples yielded 0 to 25 Y-mapping reads per sample and failed to identify either of the two animals that Rx places firmly in the male range, so we adopted the X-to-autosome ratio Rx of Mittnik et al.

items.title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
items.summary: We provide an explicit scheme to realize a quantum memory in any 2D non-chiral topological order. For this, we construct syndrome extraction circuits based on the Turaev-Viro path integral as well as a classical algorithm for decoding on the fly. We prove that our scheme has a threshold under a local stochastic circuit-level noise model and discuss how to generalize it to implement topological logical gates.
items.author: Yuanjie Ren, Margarita Davydova, Shankar Balasubramanian et al.

items.title: Joint analysis of the Macquart relation and the dispersion measure power spectrum: cross-covariance and redshift self-calibration
items.summary: The dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace ionised baryons along the line of sight, probing baryonic feedback. Two complementary observables can be constructed from an FRB catalogue: the DM-redshift (Macquart) relation of host-identified FRBs, and the angular power spectrum of the DM field of the full catalogue. Their joint analysis requires their cross-covariance. We derive it within the halo model and show it is a super-sample effect: only the monopole of an individual DM correlates with the angular power spectrum, yielding an exact, model-independent bound on the correlation coefficient. We validate the calculation against log-normal forward simulations of $10^4$ FRBs.
items.author: Amy Wayland, Robert Reischke

items.title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems
items.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision. This survey reviews these approaches using two complementary classification axes: teacher-student configuration and the role of quantum resources in the distillation process. Quantum-inspired methods are discussed separately from methods that simulate quantum computations classically or execute them on quantum hardware. We explain how measurement probabilities, expectation values, classical readouts, state overlaps, and circuit-level objectives support different transfer mechanisms. We then critically assess the presented results against baseline design, execution conditions, uncertainty, and resource costs.
items.author: Aldana Al-Sulaiti, Kuan-Cheng Chen, Muhammad Bilal Akram Dastagir et al.

items.title: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
items.summary: Quantum information systems such as quantum key distribution and quantum communications require bright, high-purity, stable sources of single photons to act as carriers of quantum information. As such, methods for obtaining single photon emitters (SPEs) in solid-state devices capable of articulating with quantum photonic circuits are a necessary obstacle that must be overcome. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) flakes have been extensively studied as a host material for SPEs, though working in two dimensions is accompanied by engineering complexity. However, dimensionality can be reduced through the implementation of boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs). Here we investigate the potential of BNNTs as room-temperature SPEs using confocal photoluminescence microscopy and Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometry.
items.author: Ke-Sean J. M. Peter, Ryan A. Kowalski, David A. Curie et al.

items.title: Testing the Spin of New Physics with Top Precision Measurements
items.summary: Precision measurements can reveal not only the presence of new physics, but also information about the dynamics that generated it. We study this question in top-pair production by comparing three top-philic scenarios: a colored scalar top partner, a colored vector-like fermion, and a spin-one $Z^\prime$ mediator. The first two contribute through loop corrections, while the $Z^\prime$ contributes at tree level. We show that the scalar and vector-like fermion scenarios match onto the same effective operator structure at low energies,making their distinction unfeasible using the EFT approach. However, near or above threshold their full loop amplitudes develop distinct momentum-dependent interference patterns.
items.author: André Lessa, Vinícius Rocca, Veronica Sanz

items.title: Dynamical effects induced by synthetic SU(1,1) gauge fields
items.summary: Compact gauge fields are powerful tools for controlling quantum dynamics and topological phases of matter. Non-compact gauge fields are particularly relevant for open systems, where particles or energy are exchanged with the environment. Here, we investigate the wavepacket and entanglement dynamics induced by an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field. The wavepacket undergoes non-Abelian non-compact Bloch oscillations, in which the spectrum of an auxiliary one-dimensional quantum problem determines the transition between stable oscillations and unstable amplification. In the unstable adiabatic regime, the wavepacket probes an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ topological defect, and its amplification is determined solely by a hyperbolic solid angle in Minkowski space. Threading an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field through a bosonic tight-binding model yields the bosonic Kitaev model, whose volume or super-volume entanglement scaling is governed by the stability of the gauge field.
items.author: Chenwei Lv

items.title: Polynomial-time classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss
items.summary: Sampling experiments are a leading approach to demonstrating quantum computational advantage, yet their robustness to experimental noise is not completely understood. We develop a common framework for classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss, including pure loss. For Fock-state boson sampling, Gaussian boson sampling with fixed uniform squeezing, and fermion sampling with magic inputs, we obtain polynomial-time sampling at inverse-polynomial total variation error, for any fixed nonzero overall loss rate, and with high probability over Haar-random interferometers. A milder flatness assumption on the ideal output distribution suffices for quasipolynomial-time simulation without Haar randomness. With constant thermal loss per layer, the same flatness assumption gives polynomial-time simulation at logarithmic depth.
items.author: Armando Angrisani, Hela Mhiri

items.title: Trapping and Fracture of Particles in Three-Sphere Ball-Milling Collisions
items.summary: We numerically investigate the collision and fracture processes of ball milling based on a minimal model of a three-sphere geometry using discrete element method (DEM) simulations combined with Christensen-type and Weibull-type normalized fracture criteria. The outcome of the brittle target particle (ejected versus trapped, fractured versus intact) depends on the impact geometry and velocity. We develop a reduced three-sphere collision description in which trapping is governed by impact geometry and friction, while fracture inside the trapping regime is evaluated from DEM output using stress-based and contact-force-based normalized criteria. The trapping regime follows a closed-form geometric condition, while the critical conditions for fracture vary with impact angle, obliquity angle, impact velocity, and particle size ratio.
items.author: Ziyi Cui, Qiong Zhang, Suwei Liu et al.

items.title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
items.summary: Designing protein sequences that satisfy both secondary structure requirements and solubility targets remains challenging. We present DiffSequence-Q, a hybrid multinomial diffusion model conditioned on secondary structure at each residue and a continuous solubility target. To introduce quantum auxiliary supervision during training, we employ a quantum neural network (QNN) or quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold network (QKAN) as an auxiliary solubility prediction head over shared Transformer representations. The auxiliary prediction loss is jointly optimized with the diffusion objective, allowing quantum auxiliary supervision to influence the learned denoising model. Once trained, protein sequences are generated entirely through classical reverse diffusion. On the CATH benchmark, DiffSequence-Q achieved the highest secondary structure recovery among the four evaluated models for complete sequence generation.
items.author: Ke-Xin Tang, Zhen-Qiang Weng, Kai Yan et al.

items.title: Can the exposome help solve the alcohol and cancer mystery?
items.summary: by Vasilis Vasiliou, Arthur Stem, David C. Thompson Alcohol consumption is a preventable driver of many cancers, yet a central biological question remains unresolved: by what mechanisms does ethanol promote malignancy? We propose that alcohol in the context of the exposome (i.e., the network of chemical, biological, and social determinants that interact with ethanol across the life span) provides a unifying framework for understanding alcohol-related carcinogenesis. Viewed through the lens of the exposome, alcohol is not only as a direct carcinogen but also as a systemic amplifier of environmental risk acting across multiple levels of biological organization, from molecular damage to whole-body physiology.
items.author: Vasilis Vasiliou, Arthur Stem, David C. Thompson

items.title: Two parallel lateral hypothalamic GABAergic projections differentially modulate pain and anxiety in mice
items.summary: by Yi-Ling Sun, Yi-Ting Peng, Xue Zhang, Cui Yin, Cheng Xiao, Junping Chen, Chunyi Zhou The lateral hypothalamus (LH) is fundamentally involved in motivated behaviors, yet the precise functional segregation of its GABAergic projections in modulating pain and its affective dimensions remains poorly understood. Here, using male and female mice, we revealed that LH GABAergic neurons sent parallel projections to two pivotal pain and affect processing centers: the lateral parabrachial nucleus (LPB) and the paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus (PVT). In vivo fiber photometry revealed that LH GABAergic terminals in both the PVT and LPB are robustly activated by noxious, aversive, and rewarding stimuli, indicating their roles in encoding salient and affective information.

items.title: Phylogenetic evidence that migratory behavior increases ungulate extinction rates
items.summary: by Joel O. Abraham, Kaedan O’Brien, Nathan S. Upham, Brett R. Jesmer, Faysal Bibi, J. Tyler Faith Widespread instances of migratory collapse have been documented within the past several decades, indicating that migration may be a fragile strategy in the Anthropocene. Yet the fragility of migration as a strategy for navigating seasonally variable resource availability may extend deeper into evolutionary time. We used phylogenetic imputation to infer the migratory habits of 51 ungulate species that went extinct during the late Quaternary and evaluated whether migration enhances extinction rates on macroevolutionary timescales. We found that ~80% (41 of 51) of recently extinct species were migratory, whereas only 46% (95 of 207) of extant ungulates are migratory.
items.author: Joel O. Abraham, Kaedan O’Brien, Nathan S. Upham et al.

items.title: TriTower-m6Am: A triple-tower heterogeneous deep learning architecture integrating semantic, sequential, and structural information for mRNA N6,2′-O-dimethyladenosine site prediction
items.summary: by Kaifeng Xiong, Jianhua Jia Background N 6 ,2′-O-dimethyladenosine (m6Am) is a cap-proximal mRNA modification deposited by PCIF1 (phosphorylated C-terminal domain (CTD)-interacting factor 1) at the first transcribed nucleotide of eukaryotic mRNAs. Knowing where m6Am sites sit would help explain how cells tune mRNA stability and translation, but current predictors typically depend on a single representation and do not jointly model multiple views of the same RNA sequence. Results We present TriTower-m6Am, combining semantic (RNA-FM, a pretrained RNA foundation model, with BellPooling), sequential (One-Hot BiLSTM, bidirectional long short-term memory), and structural (RGCN, a relational graph convolutional network, over the 41-nt window) representations of each RNA window.
items.author: Kaifeng Xiong, Jianhua Jia

items.title: A computational framework to model cartilage degeneration induced by mechanoinflammation and cytokine-driven inflammation in post-traumatic osteoarthritis
items.summary: by Moustafa Hamada, Atte S. A. Eskelinen, Joonas P. Kosonen, Sanna Hakonen, Cristina Florea, Alan J. Grodzinsky, Rami K. Korhonen, Petri Tanska Knee joint injury is a major risk factor for post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA), often associated with early cartilage degeneration. Mechanical overloading and cytokine-driven inflammation are key drivers of this process, yet the underlying mechanisms and their distinct temporal and spatial contributions to cartilage degradation remain unclear. Here, we present a mechanobiological finite element framework that simulates cartilage degradation through cell-mediated proteolytic activity triggered by injurious loading-driven mechanoinflammation and cytokine-driven inflammation. The model reproduces experimentally observed depth-dependent loss of collagen and aggrecan, with mechanoinflammation inducing a transient response and cytokine-driven inflammation sustaining prolonged matrix degradation.
items.author: Moustafa Hamada, Atte S. A. Eskelinen, Joonas P. Kosonen et al.

items.title: Ten simple rules for a successful global health roundtable
items.summary: by Maria Gabriela Uribe Guajardo, Amanda Rush, Michelle Cunich, Kathleen Cravero, Carmen Huckel Schneider Qualitative approaches play a critical role in global health research by capturing the social, political, and contextual dimensions that shape health outcomes. While interviews and focus groups are widely used, these methods are often time‑limited and project‑specific. Global health roundtables offer a complementary approach, providing a flexible and long-term platform for engaging diverse stakeholders—including researchers, practitioners, policymakers, and community representatives—in collective dialogue, knowledge exchange, and collaboration. When designed well, roundtables can support co‑production of knowledge, address complex system‑level challenges, and generate insights with relevance beyond a single event.
items.author: Maria Gabriela Uribe Guajardo, Amanda Rush, Michelle Cunich et al.

items.title: Membrane tension and cell–nucleus mechanical coupling regulate confined cell migration
items.summary: by David Hernandez-Aristizabal, Anotida Madzvamuse, Rachele Allena Cell migration is a fundamental physiological process essential from embryogenesis to cancer metastasis. It is primarily governed by the coupled mechanics of the plasma membrane (PM) and the nucleus, together with cytoskeletal dynamics. Being the largest and stiffest organelle, the nucleus is considered a rate-limiting factor in confined migration. However, nuclear positioning varies across cell types and migration modes, and the forces orchestrating its mechanical coupling with the PM are not completely understood. In recent decades, mathematical modelling has gained relevance to support cell migration research, yet models face the fundamental challenge of balancing mechanistic detail with computational efficiency.
items.author: David Hernandez-Aristizabal, Anotida Madzvamuse, Rachele Allena

items.title: Social manipulations trigger shifts in group-level dominance patterns
items.summary: by Annemarie van der Marel, Xavier Francis, Claire L. O’Connell, Cesar O. Estien, Chelsea Carminito, V. Darby Moore, Elizabeth A. Hobson Within dominance hierarchies, individuals often direct aggression based on their own rank and the rank of others. When many group members make the same rank-informed aggression decisions, a broader group-level “dominance pattern” can emerge which further structures aggression within the framework of the dominance hierarchy. However, whether groups can change their group-level dominance patterns over time, and what factors might drive these changes, are not well understood. We investigated aggression dynamics by experimentally manipulating captive groups of monk parakeets ( Myiopsitta monachus ) using targeted rank-based removals and reintroductions of group members to induce social instability.
items.author: Annemarie van der Marel, Xavier Francis, Claire L. O’Connell et al.

items.title: Genomic ascertainment refines the population prevalence and phenotype associations of germline TERT variants
items.summary: by Marena R. Niewisch, Sherifa A. Akinniyi, Kelvin C. de Andrade, Jung Kim, Logan P. Zeigler, Jeremy S. Haley, Gretchen Urban, David J. Carey, Douglas R. Stewart, Sharon A. Savage Background Individuals with deleterious germline variants in telomerase (encoded by TERT ) are at high risk of pulmonary fibrosis (PF), liver disease (LD), bone marrow failure, head/neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), and other complications. Clinically ascertained cohorts are subject to biased ascertainment of affected individuals and families with early onset, complex disease. This study used genomic ascertainment to determine prevalence of deleterious TERT variants and the associated risks of telomere biology disorder (TBD) phenotypes.
items.author: Marena R. Niewisch, Sherifa A. Akinniyi, Kelvin C. de Andrade et al.

items.title: Nitroxoline treatment of Balamuthia mandrillaris triggers genomic crisis, transcriptional collapse, and incomplete encystment via copper and iron chelation
items.summary: by Kaitlin A. Marquis, Natasha Spottiswoode, Angela M. Detweiler, Norma Neff, Joseph L. DeRisi Balamuthia mandrillaris is a free-living amoeba that can infect the central nervous system to cause granulomatous amebic encephalitis (GAE), a fatal disease with mortality rates up to 90%. GAE is typically treated with a six-drug regimen with limited efficacy and significant toxicity. Our lab previously identified nitroxoline, a quinolone antibiotic, as a promising therapeutic complement to the existing regimen, and in 2021 nitroxoline was first successfully used to treat a human patient. In this study, we elucidate nitroxoline’s mechanism of action using a combination of genomics, transcriptomics, chemical complementation, growth assays, and electron microscopy.
items.author: Kaitlin A. Marquis, Natasha Spottiswoode, Angela M. Detweiler et al.

items.title: A single-residue deletion in H9N2 hemagglutinin uncouples viral burden from disease severity
items.summary: by Yixue Sun, Yanting Zhu, Pengju Zhang, Shouzhi Sheng, Lili Gai, Siqi Li, Fangyu Zhang, Peige Cao, Ao He, Weixia Wang, Xintao Li, Yanlong Cong H9N2 avian influenza viruses are characterized by significant genetic diversity. Deletions within the hemagglutinin (HA) receptor-binding domain represent a notable, albeit rare, evolutionary trajectory. Here, we systematically characterized the multifaceted impact of a single-amino-acid deletion at residue 227 of HA (designated HA Δ227 ), a naturally occurring deletion within the 220-loop that overlaps a key antigenic epitope, using isogenic reverse genetics H9N2 viruses. Paradoxically, the HA Δ227 imposed a fitness cost and was associated with enhanced HA receptor-binding avidity, reduced apparent virion-associated NA activity, altered HA/NA functional balance, attenuated viral replication in vitro , and reduced respiratory shedding in vivo .

Llewellyn, on behalf of the CRUZIDERM Consortium , Walt Adamson, Julio Alonso-Padilla, Antonella Bacigalupo, Jean-Mathieu Bart, Bruno Bucheton, Jaime A. Costales, Anahí G.
